An agent harness, also known as agent scaffolding, is the software infrastructure surrounding a large language model (LLM) that enables it to operate as an AI agent. It manages tool use, memory, state persistence, execution environments and feedback loops, as opposed to the model's internal reasoning. The UK's AI Security Institute described an AI agent as being formed by the model plus the scaffolding back in 2023. The relationship can be expressed as agent = model + harness. Rather than repeatedly re-reading an ever-growing transcript inside the context window, a harness can offload record-keeping into a structured software environment that manages the agent's state. An AI Agent Harness is the software infrastructure that surrounds a Large Language Model (LLM) and enables it to interact with the outside world. It connects the model to tools, memory, execution environments, and safety controls, allowing the model's decisions to be translated into meaningful actions.

Simply put:

```
AI Agent = Model + Harness 
```

Think of the model as the brain that reasons and decides what should happen next. The harness is everything around it that enables those decisions to be executed safely and reliably.

A typical AI agent harness consists of four key capabilities.

## Tools

The harness connects the model to external systems, including: [...] The harness records:

 Tool calls
 Execution traces
 Latency
 Errors
 Token usage
 Workflow history

This helps developers debug, evaluate, and improve agent systems.

# Why Harness Design Matters

As LLMs become more capable, the harness becomes an increasingly important factor in agent performance.

A strong harness improves:

 Context management
 Tool orchestration
 Memory handling
 Verification
 Safety
 Reliability

In many real-world scenarios, a well-designed harness around a smaller model can outperform a more capable model with poor execution infrastructure.

The future of AI performance will depend not only on better models but also on better systems built around those models.

The root cause is architectural, not behavioral. Telling an agent `"follow our coding standards"` in a prompt is fundamentally different from wiring a linter that blocks the PR when standards are violated. The first approach relies on probabilistic compliance; the second enforces deterministic constraints. Harness engineering formalizes this distinction.

## **What Is Harness Engineering: Origin and Definition**

The term "harness engineering" is commonly attributed to Mitchell Hashimoto, co-founder of HashiCorp and creator of Terraform, in a [blog post published in early February 2026](https://mitchellh.com/writing/my-ai-adoption-journey). The original post URL has not been independently recovered, so this attribution is based on secondary reports: the core principle being that whenever an agent makes a mistake, engineers should build a solution ensuring the agent never makes that specific mistake again.

The concept gained a formal definition through an [OpenAI post](https://openai.com/index/harness-engineering/) by Ryan Lopopolo on February 11, 2026, built on the experience of shipping a production application with zero manually written lines of code. The tagline: *"Humans steer. Agents execute."* A [LangChain post](https://blog.langchain.com/the-anatomy-of-an-agent-harness/) condensed the model: *"Agent = Model + Harness."*

A common misattribution: Andrej Karpathy coined [context engineering](https://x.com/karpathy/status/2002118205729562949) (Dec 2025) and [agentic engineering](https://x.com/karpathy/status/2026731645169185220) (Feb 2026), not harness engineering.

| Term | Attributed To | Primary Source | Date |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Harness engineering | Mitchell Hashimoto (per secondary reports) | Personal blog, "My AI Adoption Journey." | Early Feb 2026 |
| Harness engineering (formal) | OpenAI / Ryan Lopopolo | openai.com/index/harness-engineering | Feb 11, 2026 |
| Agentic engineering | Andrej Karpathy | x.com/karpathy | Feb 2026 |
| Context engineering | Andrej Karpathy | x.com/karpathy | Dec 19, 2025 |

## **Harness Engineering vs. Prompt Engineering vs. Context Engineering**

Harness engineering occupies a distinct architectural layer from prompt engineering and context engineering. Understanding the boundaries prevents teams from applying single-turn techniques to multi-session, multi-agent problems.

Prompt engineering optimizes instructions for a single interaction. Context engineering curates the information passed across turns within a single context window. Harness engineering operates outside both: it introduces context resets, structured handoff artifacts, and phase gates that enable coherent, goal-directed work across multiple context windows.

An [arXiv analysis](https://arxiv.org/html/2603.05344v1) describes the harness as orchestrating tool dispatch, context management, and safety enforcement at runtime, with the tool registry and safety system as distinct components alongside the prompt composition layer.

| Dimension | Prompt Engineering | Context Engineering | Harness Engineering |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Scope | Single interaction | Model's context window across turns | Entire agent system |
| What it controls | Instruction wording | Token selection, ordering, compaction | Tool orchestration, state persistence, verification loops, error recovery |
| Failure modes addressed | Unclear instructions | Wrong or missing information in context | Agent errors, doom loops, multi-session drift, unsafe actions |
| Temporal boundary | One turn | One context window | Multiple context windows; full task lifetime |

## **The Three Harness Layers: Constraints, Feedback Loops, Quality Gates**

Harness engineering operates through reinforcing layers: preventive controls that stop unwanted outputs before they occur, and corrective controls that detect violations and trigger a response. Teams starting from zero should implement them in order: constraint harnesses first be
segments.title: Harness Engineering for AI Coding Agents: Constraints That Ship Reliable Code | Augment Code

segments.text:
cause they reduce failure volume before anything else is in place, feedback loops second because they enable self-correction without human intervention, quality gates third because they enforce what the first two layers could not prevent.

One tradeoff applies to all three: over-constraining is a real failure mode. Complexity limits set too low flag legitimate refactoring; lint rules that reject valid patterns slow agents without improving output quality. Start narrow, measure, then expand.

### **Layer 1: Constraint Harnesses (Feedforward)**

Constraint harnesses reduce the agent's solution space before generation begins. Rules files, architectural lint configurations, and type systems all function as feedforward controls. They encode what the correct code looks like, so the agent converges faster on compliant output.

[OpenAI's production system](https://openai.com/index/harness-engineering/) enforces what it calls taste invariants: a small set of rules that encode the team's engineering standards and design philosophy, including general coding conventions and reliability requirements. All are enforced as hard CI failures, not warnings.

### **Layer 2: Feedback Loops (Corrective)**

Feedback loops return structured error signals to the agent, enabling autonomous self-correction. The critical implementation detail is that the lint message itself becomes a prompt. A lint error saying `"violation detected"` requires human interpretation. A lint error saying `use logger.info({event: 'name', ...data}) instead of console.log` enables the agent to fix the violation without human intervention.

One implementation detail most teams overlook: inline-disable rules, such as `// eslint-disable-next-line`, should be disabled to prevent agents from suppressing violations rather than fixing them.

### **Layer 3: Quality Gates (Enforcement)**

Quality gates prevent non-compliant code from being merged. Standard CI pipelines are insufficient for AI-generated code because agents introduce problems that conventional checks miss. Some teams add purpose-built staleness gates to catch dependency choices that do not match the codebase's current strategy.

javascript

```


// .eslintrc.js: Structural constraints for AI-generated code



module.exports = {



rules: {



"complexity": ["error", { "max": 10 }],



"max-depth": ["error", 4],



"max-lines-per-function": ["error", { "max": 50 }],



"max-lines": ["error", { "max": 300 }],



"max-params": ["error", 4],



"max-statements": ["error", 15]



}



}


```

All rules set to `"error"`, not `"warn"`, so they function as hard gates, not advisory signals.

## **Rules Files as Constraint Harnesses**

Rules files are persistent, repository-scoped instruction sets injected into an agent's context at session start. The mechanical distinction from simple prompts is precise: rules files survive across sessions, are injected automatically by the runtime, scope to an entire directory tree, and compose hierarchically across parent and child directories.

### **The Cross-Tool Landscape**

The `AGENTS.md` [spec](https://agents.md/), released in August 2025 as an open standard emerging from collaboration across the AI coding ecosystem, including OpenAI, Google, Cursor, Factory, and others, now functions as a shared cross-tool convention. [OpenAI's repository](https://developers.openai.com/codex/guides/agents-md) uses 88 `AGENTS.md` files across subcomponents, demonstrating monorepo-scale constraint composition.

| Tool | File | Scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| OpenAI Codex | AGENTS.md | Hierarchical, Git root to CWD |
| Claude Code | CLAUDE.md | Project root + ~/.claude |
| Cursor | .cursor/rules/\*.mdc | Project-scoped |
| GitHub Copilot | .github/copilot-instructions.md | Repo-wide + path-specific |
| Cosmos | AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, plus native Augment Rules | Cross-tool compatible |

### **Augment Rules: Three-Type Constraint Architecture**

Cosmos implements a rules system called Augment Rules with three

segments.text:
ernetics) governor, combining feed-forward and feedback to regulate the codebase towards its desired state. It's useful to distinguish between multiple dimensions of that desired state, categorised by what the harness is supposed to regulate. Distinguishing between these categories helps because harnessability and complexity vary across them, and qualifying the word gives us more precise language for a term that is otherwise very generic.

The following are three categories that seem useful to me as of now:

### Maintainability harness

More or less all of the examples I am giving in this article are about regulating internal code quality and maintainability. This is at the moment the easiest type of harness, as we have a lot of pre-existing tooling that we can use for this.

To reflect on how much these aforementioned maintainability harness ideas increase my trust in agents, I mapped [common coding agent failure modes that I catalogued before](https://martinfowler.com/articles/exploring-gen-ai/13-role-of-developer-skills.html) against it.

Computational sensors catch the structural stuff reliably: duplicate code, cyclomatic complexity, missing test coverage, architectural drift, style violations. These are cheap, proven, and deterministic.

LLMs can partially address problems that require semantic judgment - semantically duplicate code, redundant tests, brute-force fixes, over-engineered solutions - but expensively and probabilistically. Not on every commit.

Neither catches reliably some of the higher-impact problems: Misdiagnosis of issues, overengineering and unnecessary features, misunderstood instructions. They'll sometimes catch them, but not reliably enough to reduce supervision. Correctness is outside any sensor's remit if the human didn't clearly specify what they wanted in the first place.

### Architecture fitness harness

This groups guides and sensors that define and check the architecture characteristics of the application. Basically: [Fitness Functions](https://www.thoughtworks.com/en-de/radar/techniques/architectural-fitness-function).

Examples:

*   Skills that feed forward our performance requirements, and performance tests that feed back to the agent if it improved or degraded them.
*   Skills that describe coding conventions for better observability (like logging standards), and debugging instructions that ask the agent to reflect on the quality of the logs it had available.

### Behaviour harness

This is the elephant in the room - how do we guide and sense if the application functionally behaves the way we need it to? At the moment, I see most people who give high autonomy to their coding agents do this:

*   Feed-forward: A functional specification (of varying levels of detail, from a short prompt to multi-file descriptions)
*   Feed-back: Check if the AI-generated test suite is green, has reasonably high coverage, some might even monitor its quality with mutation testing. Then combine that with manual testing.

This approach puts a lot of faith into the AI-generated tests, that's not good enough yet. Some of my colleagues are seeing good results with the [approved fixtures](https://lexler.github.io/augmented-coding-patterns/patterns/approved-fixtures/) pattern, but it's easier to apply in some areas than others. They use it selectively where it fits, it's not a wholesale answer to the test quality problem.

So overall, we still have a lot to do to figure out good harnesses for functional behaviour that increase our confidence enough to reduce supervision and manual testing.

# Feedback loop engineering

![Hero image](/_next/image?url=%2Fimages%2F2026%2Floop-the-loop-luna-park-coney-island-84d581.jpg&w=3840&q=75)
![avatar](/_next/image?url=%2Fimages%2Fdain.jpg&w=96&q=75)

A while back I listened to [a Pragmatic Engineer podcast with Peter Steinberger](https://newsletter.pragmaticengineer.com/p/the-creator-of-clawd-i-ship-code) about his AI-native development workflow – the one where he runs 5-10 coding agents in parallel and ships code he doesn't personally read. The headline numbers are easy to fixate on, but what stuck with me was the infrastructure underneath them. His workflow doesn't succeed because he writes better prompts, or even because he feeds the agents better context. It works because he's built what he calls "closed-loop systems" where the agents verify their own work – compiling, running, debugging, screenshotting, hitting real API keys.

I've been chewing on that pattern ever since, and I think it deserves its own name. Here's my current hierarchy:

Prompt engineering < context engineering < feedback loop engineering < harness engineering

## The four levels

**Prompt engineering** is where most people start – and where most of the discourse lies. How do you phrase your request? What system prompt works best? Should I write "please" or "my job depends on it, make no mistakes"? It might matter, but the models are getting good enough to infer intention from vague prompts. Instead of crafting the perfect spec and trying to cover all possibilities, you can just have a conversation.

**Context engineering** is the next step up. This is about giving the model the right information: a well-crafted `CLAUDE.md` / `AGENTS.md`, relevant documentation, carefully selected files in the context window. I [wrote about some of my practices here](/blog/my-coding-agent-workflows) – things like using Plan mode and including the most relevant files upfront. Context engineering gets you much further than prompt engineering alone because the model stops guessing blind. It can also fill in the gaps much more easily from existing practice rather than assumptions.

`CLAUDE.md`
`AGENTS.md`

But **feedback loop engineering** is what separates working code from getting lucky. It's the practice of building tools and infrastructure so that coding agents can verify their work *in context*. Not to stop when they did a reasonable amount of work and feel like it's "production ready", but to see hard evidence of how the code behaves in an as production-like setup as possible.

**Harness engineering** is the frame around all of it. Birgitta Böckeler [defines the harness as everything in an agent except the model itself](https://martinfowler.com/articles/harness-engineering.html) – "Agent = Model + Harness" – and splits it into *guides* that steer the agent before it acts (feedforward: your `CLAUDE.md`, types, linting) and *sensors* that let it observe the consequences after (feedback: the loops I'll get to below). By that definition my "feedback loop engineering" is really the sensor half of harness engineering, done on purpose.

`CLAUDE.md`

So why give it its own rung rather than fold it in? Because the three answer different questions. Context engineering is about what goes *in*. Harness engineering is about governing the whole apparatus – which tools the agent can call, what it's allowed to touch, when it should stop. And the feedback loop is the connective tissue between them: the bit that decides whether the agent ever finds out it was wrong. It's also, I'd argue, where most developers get the best return on their time today. And for people using closed source harnesses like Claude Code or Cursor, the term harness engineering might sound confusing when it's only adding some skills or hooks.

## What this looks like in practice

The core idea is straightforward: you want the agent to be able to run its code, see the result, and iterate. Just like a developer would. The faster and tighter that loop, the better the
segments.title: Feedback loop engineering

segments.text:
a single session. Tighten that loop and the output gets better. But there's a slower, wider loop sitting on top of it, and it's where the compounding really happens.

The **outer loop** is what turns one session's hard-won lesson into something every future session starts with. An agent burns half an hour discovering that a particular API silently truncates payloads over a certain size, or that a migration needs a specific flag on this database version. In the inner loop that knowledge lives and dies inside the context window. In the outer loop it gets reflected on at the end of the session, distilled, and written back into the shared knowledge the next agent loads up front – a new skill, a note in `CLAUDE.md`, an entry in a team knowledge base.

`CLAUDE.md`

Mozilla AI's [`cq`](https://github.com/mozilla-ai/cq) is the cleanest take on this I've seen. It's an open standard for shared agent learning: agents store discoveries as structured "knowledge units" – undocumented API quirks, workarounds, fixes – and *query the store before retrying a failure*, so they stop rediscovering the same dead ends independently. A `/cq:reflect` command mines a finished session for the lessons worth keeping, ranks them by how generalisable they are, checks for duplicates, and proposes new units for you to approve. The store can live locally in SQLite or sync across a whole team. Their own framing names it exactly: separate the inner loop of solving the problem from the outer loop of consolidating what you learned.

`cq`
`/cq:reflect`

The neat part is how the two loops join up. Today's distilled lesson becomes tomorrow's *guide* – feedforward, in harness terms – so the outer loop quietly improves the inner one over time. It's the same circle a good team already runs: someone debugs a gnarly issue, writes it up, and the next person doesn't have to start from scratch. We're just teaching the agents to do their own write-ups.

## The best bit

What I like about this approach is that feedback loop engineering isn't just AI-specific overhead. Observability, structured logging, trace correlation, browser testing, database verification, clear interfaces, helpful error messages – these were good engineering practices long before anyone was prompting a language model. The difference is that wrapping them as CLI-accessible skills makes them available to agents too. The feedback loops that help an agent debug a cross-service issue are the same ones that help a developer on their first week understand how the system actually behaves.

So if you're wondering where to invest your time as AI coding tools improve: less time crafting the perfect prompt, more time building tools that let agents – and humans – see what's actually happening. The prompts and coding agent harnesses will change as models evolve. The value of a tight feedback loop won't. And if the AI bubble pops next month, you're left with easy to test codebases that you can pick up again yourself or use local models for smaller tasks. If it doesn't, the inner and outer loops keep compounding, and your agents get a little less forgetful with every session.

And for Pete's sake, [don't install OpenClaw connected to all your personal data and services...](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/eracle_aiagents-promptinjection-moltbot-activity-7423126588160012289-Wcjg)

贵圈太乱。明明之前，说跟郑爽很多话聊的，也是许晴自己：“郑爽是个特别可爱的90后妹子，和她蛮有缘分，有很多私房话要聊。旅行中从郑爽身上可以看见当年的自己。”啪啪啪，前方谁在打脸，好大声。

　　如果对象是男人 不会轻易撕脸？ 也有网友扒出疑似许晴跟郑爽撕逼的真正原因，说的是开车的路上，本来陈意涵郑爽宁静杨洋一个房车，毛毛姐许晴井宝一个车，开始三个人还有说有笑，中途在休息站停了下，后来井柏然就上了郑爽杨洋的车，开始讨论行程。那么房车上就是郑爽井宝陈意涵杨洋宁静，理所当然，另外一辆车就剩下许晴跟毛阿敏姐了。万能的网友表示许晴很不爽：“看过直播的表示，许晴一直把井宝当成私人物品，嫉妒井宝去了杨洋那辆车不回来了，然后找茬大爆发。对男生、对女生态度千差万别，对三个女生好凶！”“许晴一直贴着毛阿敏，因为毛阿敏宠她，不管真假，起码给她个面子。就像上季凯丽一样，虽然晕乎乎没什么能力，但是她宠许晴，所以许晴一直贴着她。井柏然是很会调节气氛的一个人，他本能地也想照顾每个人的情绪，这是他的一种习惯。他如果再往郑爽宁静陈意涵那边，就太冷落许晴和毛阿敏了，所以他一直在两个团体里游走。”

　　网友也是很有道理的。在一期《快乐大本营》中，许晴对张翰的眼神，爱意满溢，她的眼里只有他，还说“只有翰从始至终选了她”，一口一个翰可亲密了。

　　细看她的微博，这一季的嘉宾中只关注了两个男孩，在节目中也是猛夸两个男孩。许晴接受采访时候曾说过：“我一直特别霸道地说，喜欢我的人一定都是善良健康的，不喜欢的一定不健康，一定不善良。”45岁的许晴依然有着18岁以下的少女心和公主病，全世界都要围着她转的自我。

　　对比上一季和这一季，嘉宾名单都有许晴，还都有许晴大哭的场面。碰到挫折后许晴在镜头前失控大哭：“我真的真的想回家。”原来长得美，是真可以任性的。这不是公主病的话，什么才是？ [...] 也许是想缓和气氛(效果真没有)，井柏然补充问一句，为什么是上一季？完全不谙世事的少女许晴开始开外挂：“因为上一季的人都正常。”人畜无害的陈意涵开始傻笑(此处省略一串哈哈哈哈哈哈)，郑爽的表情则是嘴角下弯的尴尬。陈意涵接着问，那什么原因让你愿意来两次。许大姐说：“因为剧组让我来。”一天之内许晴微博10万条评论，除了脑残粉之外全是骂她的。

　　上一季，她和刘涛不和的消息就没停止过，微博上也取消关注了从中说和的郑佩佩。现在又说第一季的人正常，也不知道到底谁不正常。

　　其实早在第一季，许晴因为档期原因，提早退出了花少团，还与大家依依惜别说：“如果有第二季，愿意再度出行，且零片酬加盟。”提到第三季，她似乎还是激情满满：“大家看第二季谁要是留级了，就是因为表现不及格。如果我还没有及格，我还会来第三季的。”

　　果然，看来是及格不了了。网上几乎一边倒的态势在骂许晴：“花儿与少年，其实郑爽的问题没有错，许晴没给小辈起码的尊重，错之一；许晴说，至少上一季的人都正常，情商出演负值，错之二；没有团队精神，没有大局意识，不能包容忍耐，不会换位思考，错之三。现在，许晴黑历史，郑爽退出花少，许晴骂郑爽……纷纷上热搜，许晴将郑爽拉下水遭受质疑，许晴你真的炸了。”

　　冰冻三尺非一日之寒。郑爽自己也说过：“我跟晴姐之间，一直有一些误会，我是觉得自己一直没有去沟通得很好。”其中一个心结，大概是杨洋走丢之后，许晴说要去找杨洋，郑爽以为杨洋有地址不会丢就说不用去。之后郑爽下楼拿外卖，许晴就以为郑爽是去接杨洋给自己加戏，开始不爽郑爽，什么解释也听不进去。许晴直接坦白地说：“她说的话我听不懂，费那个心思再去聊天。” [...] 中新网 • 文娱 • 正文

# 许晴《花少2》中表现遭批 被质疑有“公主病”

纽约时间6月7日，许晴身穿淡蓝色纱裙亮相2015托尼奖颁奖礼红毯，成为首位踏上托尼奖红毯的中国女星。

　　她在微博晒出美照并附言：“不因现实的乌云，而背离戏剧的光彩；不以世界的复杂，而背叛内心的纯粹。”疑似对负面新闻作出回应。

　　画风变得实在太快。参加第二季《花儿与少年》的初始，许晴还在美滋滋地说着爱情的话题，“她笑称参加完第二季之后，目前正在从女生向‘柔软的美男子’进化，更重要的是这次疯狂的旅行也让她深深地爱上了一起搭错地铁、一起深夜迷路的小伙伴们，她正陷入一场和每个人的热恋。”“对两次旅行的导游，许晴形容郑爽像小妈妈，而张翰更像哥哥：郑爽会细心地帮她把地铁卡收到小包里，而面对做事比较霸气的哥哥，有小意外可以顶撞他。”一副和美的景象不忍破坏。

　　前后不到一个月，关于许晴的黑话题又上了话题榜。负面来得太快就像龙卷风。

上一季矫揉这一季自我

撒娇女人未必最好命

　　在最新播出的《花儿与少年》中，播了一段大家伙玩真心话的片段，郑爽开始问许晴，到底是这一季开心还是上一季开心啊？这么正常的套近乎，却惹来许晴不正常的回答：“上一季。”没有一点点防备，也没有一丝顾虑，她就这样回答，斩钉截铁。当时人家就震惊了，也惹恼了紧追剧情的观众，许晴微博下面的评论一片叫骂，“做作”“负能量”的字眼满屏皆是。本来还黏在许晴身上的井柏然当时一下子就起来了，神情尴尬。许晴还咬了下嘴唇，场面一度僵持，感觉许晴内心一定是：说了就说了你们怎么着吧。

结果郑爽来了一句：我哪都不爱住。 这句话让许晴很不爽，许晴本身就不喜欢郑爽，一句话都懒得搭理，来找她是解决问题的，而不是听郑爽说撒娇话的。

说完自己想住帐篷后，许晴和毛阿敏准备开着车去买吃的，毕竟是户外露营。

许晴找到郑爽后，让郑爽她们把房车上的箱子拿下来，她们要开着房车去超市。

郑爽表示：这地方好脏。

宁静也帮助好姐妹郑爽：这灰特别大。言下之意：我们就不搬箱子。

而在一旁的毛阿敏并不知情，还对许晴说：我们开房车去买吃的，也要把车上的箱子拿下来啊。（箱子本身就是要拿下来的，晚上要露营，而且车重会耗油）

许晴撒气的说：她们不拿，说有灰，我真搞不懂。

说完后，许晴又对着毛阿敏吐槽：我问她们想住哪里，她们说随便，哪里都行，那帐篷就我们住吧，烦死人了。

郑爽错失帐篷，宁静拉着郑爽走到一旁，开始商量怎么把帐篷夺回来。

许晴在事后吐槽郑爽、宁静、陈意涵姐妹团，许晴说：我有点高估我自己，我有点累，那种累是因为一件很简单的事，她们说随便随便，让简单的事情复杂化，我特别不欣赏这样。

许晴还说：这个旅行还有九天才结束，我也不想逼着自己做那些她们觉得正常的行为。

我其实能理解许晴的心情，跟郑爽说话永远不在一个点上，郑爽永远在东拉西扯，一点也不真实，而许晴最反感虚伪。

吐槽归吐槽，在许晴说帐篷归自己和毛阿敏住以后，郑爽去打电话给爸妈，在电话里，郑爽说：晚上可能住帐篷吧。（看来郑爽心里还是放不下帐篷，势必要夺回来）

天色渐渐暗下来了，宁静看到制作方的帐篷，直接问：能住三个人吗？可以给我们吗？

宁静拿到帐篷后，还假意客套一番说：如果能睡三个人就睡女的，如果只能睡两个人，就睡男的。意思是：这不是为我搬过来的啊，我们很谦让，我们随意。

结果，车上还真的只找到两个睡袋，也就是说，这个帐篷归杨洋和井柏然睡了。

此时，许晴才姗姗来迟，她才知道宁静已经安排好了住宿，自己的提议被推翻了。

如果按照许晴的提议，是她和毛阿敏睡帐篷。但宁静直接推翻不认，说了N句随便后，又要求自己和郑爽、陈意涵睡帐篷。但如意算盘落空了，只有2个睡袋。于是帐篷只能让杨洋和井柏然睡。五个女人要一起睡在房车里。

许晴不愿意和抱团三姐妹睡在一起，说想安静一下。

于是，许晴直接在一辆小汽车的后座铺了个床，决定一个人度过一夜。

没多久，毛阿敏在房车上又多发现了一个睡袋，拿给了宁静。此刻，有了三个睡袋，宁静和郑爽如愿以偿的睡到了帐篷，还拉着陈意涵一起。

井柏然告诉许晴：她们三个住在帐篷里，不睡车上了。

许晴说：那好吧，我就回房车住了。

事后，陈意涵接受采访说：郑爽很想睡帐篷，她觉得住在车上很危险， 很多人在车上睡觉死了。

宁静的表现就更搞笑了，在镜头前说自己想睡在房车上。

宁静还表示：是陈意涵和郑爽想睡在帐篷，尤其是郑爽，要求一定不能主在车上。言下之意，宁静是为了陪着两姐妹才委屈住在帐篷里的。

人间作精宁静，这不行那不行，又作又想走耿直人设，“耿直”不是遮羞布，心机才是真的。

这段视频是两年后在网上火起来的，很多人觉得这是许晴洗白自己放出来的，但并不是。很搞笑，这段视频是郑爽的粉丝放出来的，为了是撕宁静，说宁静是两面派，坑郑爽。结果郑爽的两面派也被网友们发现了，这就是亲自给偶像招黑吧？

许晴拒绝共同用餐

通过抢帐篷事件，许晴更加认识到郑爽和宁静的两副面孔，很排斥她俩。抢帐篷的第二天，七个人要去吃午饭。

许晴直接不下车，不想跟三姐妹坐在一起，在车上等着大家吃完。

毛阿敏也心知肚明许晴不爽，于是说：那我给你打包一点吃的吧。

许晴坚持说：我真不吃。

大家津津有味的享用午饭

许晴真的不愿意吃饭吗？等到花少团吃完后，她跑到咖啡厅去享受食物了。她不是不饿，只是不想和抱团三姐妹坐在一起。

当时井柏然周旋在5个女人中间，直接急的叫了起来：无所谓，爱咋咋地吧，通过这一次，我对女人有新的了解。

试问，许晴有没有错。她有，她最大的错就是太拧巴，错在以为自己无所不能，以为真人秀里能交到真心的朋友，但当发现气场不对，没必要和她们成为朋友时，她连演都不想演，导致大家都被她的言语和行为弄得尴尬和小心翼翼，这是她最大的问题。

彻底撕破脸的篝火晚会

如果说房车事件是整个节目的高潮，那篝火晚会就是她们的决裂。

在抢帐篷后的第二天，花少团继续露营，宁静开心的扎帐篷

然而，郑爽坐在一旁默不作声，若有所思。

郑爽为什么心事重重的样子呢？因为连续两天晚上都要选房车和帐篷。虽然郑爽第一天如愿以偿的睡到了帐篷，但第二天起床后就担心晚上帐篷会被许晴抢走了。

于是郑爽刚起床就跟宁静、陈意涵说：我们还是继续睡帐篷吧，别想了。

陈意涵点头：那就说我们要睡帐篷。郑爽告诉她：我们就说睡出经验来了，有什么好说的啊？

佩服佩服，睡觉还能睡出经验来

房车之旅的第二天晚上，大家围在一起吃饭，旁边还有一堆篝火，毛阿敏提议玩真心话大冒险的游戏。这一段谈话非常的负能量和低气压。

宁静问井柏然：你最累的地方是什么？

井柏然说：大家都有自己的想法，有自己想做的事情，比如分房睡，我觉得是个很简单的事，大家弄得很复杂。大家都在说随便，到底是真的随便还是假的随便，我已经分不清了。最后，大家产生了很多误会。

杨洋问井柏然：这种情绪影响你多久了？

井柏然说：至今为止都会影响我，我今天已经快崩溃了。

井柏然又问陈意涵：你觉得这段旅行最沮丧的原因是什么？

陈意涵说：这个旅行和我想的不太一样。这两天一直有点事情，我也不晓得为什么。

陈意涵的意思是，他原本以为旅行会很轻松很美好，没想到如此的心累，这两天7个人里面有很多误会、排挤、冷落和争吵。

杨洋问郑爽：你觉得我们团队是刚开始融洽还是现在融洽？

郑爽说现在融洽。这句话也太假了··· 刚开始大家好歹还假客套一下，现在一个篝火晚会这么负能量，抢帐篷又这么心机，你跟我说融洽？

这次轮到每个人都问郑爽一个问题，大家让许晴提问，许晴直接说：我没有问题。这让本来就很冷的气氛变得更冷。

许晴说：有些人还是得有距离，真的不想再说第二句话，七个人的性格都不一样，要拼命融合在一起，又不可能融合，我真的好孤独。（这些话是后续采访时补上的）

现场的气氛很尴尬，轮到了大家问许晴问题。郑爽问：晴姐，你上季玩的开心还是这一季开心呀？

其实郑爽问这种问题真是没事找事，明知道许晴不喜欢她了还问，难不成非想看看许晴怎么发飙？得，许晴终于发飙了，气氛更尴尬了，就想问她为啥没事找事？

许晴不假思索的说：上一季。

本来依偎在许晴身边的井柏然惊恐的坐了起来，问许晴：为什么是上一季？

许晴说：因为上一季的人都正常。许晴四十多岁了，没有结婚生子，活在自己构想的艺术少女世界里。她对人际交往有种不切实际的高要求，拒绝市侩、讨巧、精明的交际。她真的不懂人情世故吗？她懂。她知道当自己说出这些话时现场气氛会更尴尬，但她不愿意虚伪的说那些。

毛阿敏一直坐在许晴身边，笑而不语的看着许晴说完了这些。我不喜欢毛阿敏这个做事风格，遇到团队成员之间的矛盾只会看热闹看笑话，很多事情争执不下时，往往大姐需要出来做出决定或者是处理矛盾，而不是袖手旁观。

当年这段播出时，很多人骂许晴。有些网友的识人眼光还是需要修炼。遇到那种敌对写在脸上的人你反而不用太担心，明枪易躲暗箭难防。反而是精于世故、平时看热闹、关键时刻做好人、好处全占齐的人才是应该最提防的。

宁静一直没有参加篝火晚会，看到导演拍的现场播放，感慨一句：怎么那么严肃的话题啊？

据说当时杨洋也说了一句话，但节目组为了突出许晴和郑爽的矛盾，那段话没有放出来。杨洋说的是：我在这里并不快乐，因为每个人都是冰冷的。

后续采访时，宁静也很不满许晴，她说：有跟自己个性不一样的人在身边，就那么不舒服吗？那有没有想过，我在别人身边，别人也会不舒服我呢？

我说难听点，如果说宁静和许晴是两坨各不相干的shi，那郑爽就是那根搅屎棍，没有她在中间瞎作，宁静和许晴压根不会有正面冲突。

篝火晚会上，每个人心里都有鬼，有的人把这趟旅行当个秀敷衍了事，比如郑爽和宁静，嘴上说一套，心里想一套。但有的人把这次当成旅行相处真情实感，比如许晴，该说什么就是什么，明知道气氛全掌握在自己的一句话，却依然不违心说话。

郑爽和宁静暗戳戳的内涵小彩蛋

许晴已经在明面上撕宁静、郑爽、陈意涵的小团体了，小团体当然也不会放过许晴。

某天晚上，宁静在敷面膜，郑爽在一旁跟宁静聊天：你看晴姐不是第二次来了嘛，让她当导游不是更好吗？有经验了，当导演是最见证能力的，她肯定也想锻炼自己，不然她为什么要来呢？下一站我们推荐一下许晴当导游吧。

宁静在旁边和郑爽一唱一和。

郑爽还明知故问：她会不会怕自己做不好啊？

宁静回：谁都怕自己做不好。

当导游是件很累的事，郑爽经常说自己在英国给大家当导游时很崩溃，井柏然也说自己当导游很累。郑爽心知肚明这些，却依然笑嘻嘻的提议许晴当导游，你觉得她是抱着什么态度去提的呢？

老大姐毛阿敏的哭泣晚餐

我们再来说说毛阿敏，毛阿敏和许晴也不是多好的朋友，不过是在一群心怀鬼胎的人里互相取暖的一对。但当许晴和别人发生一些矛盾，你又被迫选择跟她站在一边，这就导致你和其他人的疏远，根本不利于正常的友谊发展。

于是，在篝火晚会事件后后，毛阿敏在饭桌上冷落了许晴，向宁静、陈意涵和郑爽大献殷勤。

许晴很看不惯，直接离席走人了。

许晴为什么走？她的回答是：我觉得那个大桌

# 回顾花儿与少年第二季，它是如何从温馨崩成噩梦的？

2019-12-06 21:58  来源: [Buy遍全球1004](//www.sohu.com)

周末大瓜 越吃越香

hello 宝贝们

今晚有局的入局 有场的上场

打麻将的杠上花 吃火锅的乐哈哈

本文很长 默默吃读需30分钟

与闺蜜边探讨边吃 需要1小时

钻进被窝 泡好茶水 我们开始吧

宁静不想去，因为在倒时差，很困，所以说：我现在眼睛都睁不开。

毛阿敏很快也站队，表示自己想睡觉。

郑爽就说：那伦敦桥可以不去的啊。（注意看，此时坐在杨洋身边的许晴不在，估计是去上洗手间了）

宁静一听，那敢情好啊！就说：不去最好（这时候许晴依然没回来）

然而，当许晴回来后，郑爽又开始另一套说辞了：我们如果今天不去伦敦桥，就错失了这个机会，明天后天都不可能再去了，这趟旅行也没可能再去了，挺可惜的。

许晴支持郑爽的导游工作，于是开口说：大家坚持一下吧！

我觉得许晴也是不想去的，但她在支持郑爽的工作。为什么这样说呢？我看过第一季，许晴有点“懒”，逛景点方面她并不积极。她是带着“都说我第一季不懂事，第二季那我就懂事给你看，我多会做和事佬啊，我多会调节气氛啊，苦就苦一点，我要扭转观众对我的看法”的想法来的，所以特别好说话，帮郑爽打圆场。

毛阿敏很快再次倒戈，表示大家走吧，去玩伦敦桥。杨洋和陈意涵听长辈的意见，所以很快就变成宁静一个人不想去了。

宁静彻底不高兴的甩脸色了，当着大家面说：明天早上谁也不要喊我，我起得来就起，起不来也别喊我。说完就往前走，也没等别人。

许晴有点被吓到，于是做了个双手投降的工作。

结果走到餐厅门外，宁静又开始摆脸色：我不玩，我也不参加了！

郑爽有点不知好歹，硬往枪口上撞，对怒气冲冲的宁静说：我觉得最好什么活动大家都一起参加，这样比较好。

郑爽还是太天真了，宁静这架势哪是你一句话就能说服的？宁静依然摆脸色不为所动，于是郑爽开始劝她：我不能让你带着不好的情绪开始旅行。

郑爽话还没说完，宁静就开始怼她：不要！不要！不要（这样说）！什么叫我有这样的情绪，昨天你还在哭鼻子呢！

当时看节目时，大家觉得是宁静在撕郑爽，其实并不是这样，她是不喜欢许晴的提议，但毕竟都是年纪相仿的女明星，不好撕，而郑爽又没有眼力见，总往枪口上撞，于是宁静顺势把怒火撒到了郑爽身上。

年纪最大的毛阿敏在一旁默默看着她俩吵架。

当天晚上，毛阿敏解释：我觉得那个时候是劝不住的，还不如让她说出来舒服一点。

毛阿敏这个人怎么说呢？作为团队里面唯一一个辈份和年纪较大的人，根本就没有做到带头和把控的作用，反而是最先挑起事端的，把自己想要的、想说的，通过旁敲侧击，鼓动旁边的人去做成。也许你觉得八哥这样说有点敏感了，不信咱们接着往下看。

当天晚上，宁静接受采访说：某些人和稀泥，你懂吗？当有一个人说最好还是去吧，结果大家都去了，谁都有性格的，我不喜欢这样。

宁静生气是因为一开始大家也表示不想去伦敦桥，结果后来许晴出来打圆场，毛阿敏也改口说要去，“耿直”的静姐一下子就炸了：明明你们一个个都不想去，现在又做起好人来劝我，搞得好像大家都通情达理，就我一个人事儿最多！她不爽的不是郑爽，而是和事佬许晴。

在这一阶段，宁静闹事，被孤立。

这个时候，许晴是对郑爽的态度比较好的，郑爽还主动和许晴提起张翰。

许晴也跟郑爽说了很多关于张翰的事情。当时在花少一的时候，郑爽和张翰要分手，张翰对着许晴和张凯丽倾诉了很多。许晴告诉郑爽：张翰对你是很认真的，他很爱你。

郑爽反驳的回了一句：最爱的人永远不在一起（那时候她已经和胡彦斌在一起了）

杨洋的伦敦街头孤单之旅

后来花少团在伦敦的街头玩枕头大战

玩结束后，郑爽犯了洁癖，大家要往前走，郑爽要整理身上的白色绒毛

伦敦的街头非常冷，郑爽让大家等了很久很久（后来节目播出时，有节目组的人在网上发帖，证实过真的等了非常久）

因为等得太久，有一幕，杨洋和郑爽对话，结果杨洋都快翻白眼了

最后，井柏然出来打圆场，为了让气氛不那么冷，就主动喊着许晴、宁静、毛阿敏她们去咖啡厅买咖啡喝。

这个时候，大家真的都非常冷

虽然大家都有点小意见了，但郑爽依然没有眼力见，他们要去下一个景点，郑爽催着杨洋导航，带路。

说实话，郑爽的为人处事和讲话方式就很难不造成冲突，杨洋又有点摆脸色了。

郑爽自己让大家等了那么久，完了又不停的催催催

杨洋有点带着情绪的说：往回走，说了好几遍了。

结果郑爽来了一句：你tm快点领路啊。没错，说脏话了，但消音了。郑爽的心不坏，但她的表达和脑回路增加了很多交流的困难，真的很难不生气。

当天晚上，大家在桌上吃饭时，一起看白天游玩的照片。

杨洋坐在一旁有点低气压，宁静这时候也不跟大家玩

后来杨洋接受采访时说：我觉得有点孤单。

伦敦之行就在宁静的暴躁和杨洋的心灵孤单中结束了，接下来他们去了剑桥。

许晴和宁静的初次不和

在剑桥旅行时，大家一起学划船。此时，许晴和杨洋、郑爽、一个英国人组成了四人队伍划船。

划完船后，许晴特别开心，说：我们四个人特别齐心。

节目组问：今天你和大家配合的好吗？许晴说：好呀，这就是团队精神。

结果四人团队换成八人团队时，许晴的心情不一样了。她的身后坐着宁静，宁静也一脸不高兴。

许晴接受采访时说：八个人时，配合不好。每个人的性格和要做的东西都很杂乱。

如果单单是因为人数多了不好配合，那也没必要说性格问题吧？可以看出此时，许晴也有点不喜欢宁静了。八哥前面说了，宁静也不喜欢许晴这个和事佬。

杨洋走丢事件，郑爽和许晴的决裂

划船后，郑爽做了一个很不好的决定，她们要回酒店，但有些人还要接受节目组的采访，于是七个人分批走。

郑爽、毛阿敏、井柏然和陈意涵第一批接受完采访后，只剩下宁静、杨洋和许晴三个人了。

这三个人里，宁静最早收工，她要司机先送自己回去，然后再回来接许晴。她不想等许晴，不过嘴上没说出来。

等到许晴结束收工时，司机告诉她：你的同伴宁静想先回去，所以没有等你。

此外，司机也告诉许晴：其他六个人都已经到酒店了，只剩你了。（其实杨洋还没走，司机搞错了）

当时许晴就很不高兴了，采访时直言：我们七个人应该在一起，如果你们四个人要先走，为什么不能等我们半个小时？

宁静谈起这个事情说：我以为许晴对我不开心了。

其实宁静的直觉没有错，许晴的确有点不高兴，也直言：宁静不应该先回来。

如果只是这样，那这个七人旅行团还能维持表面的平和。但是，杨洋被落单了。

许晴回来后找杨洋，结果发现杨洋没回来。

许晴当下立断和井柏然说：我们去接杨洋吧！

正当许晴和井柏然准备去接杨洋时，郑爽来劝他们不要去接杨洋。郑爽：他有我们的地址，所以他肯定会找回来的。

许晴反问：那万一杨洋没拿地址呢？

郑爽坚持：他拿了地址的。（郑爽你怎么就确定杨洋拿了地址呢？）

许晴还是不放心，所以说：他连电话都没有，万一没地址怎么办？

（这个节目在录制前把嘉宾们的私人物品全部收走了，只留了两台手机备用，杨洋没有手机）

不管郑爽如何劝，许晴还是坚持要接杨洋回来。

但郑爽依然在旁边坚持自己的观点：我觉得肯定丢不了，他那么大的人了。

再次说一句，郑爽真的太固执了，习惯性的反驳别人。

毛阿敏说：不是说丢不丢的问题，主要是把他落单了，心里过意不去。

郑爽坚持杨洋有地址，那但事实上杨洋没带钱，没有iPad查导航，也没有地址。

此时，天真的杨洋还在想：我不能走，我要留在原地，万一我走了，姐姐们派车来接我，找不到我怎么办？

陈意涵这时候开始打电话，联系她们走之前去划船的那个俱乐部，准备打听消息。然而俱乐部已经下班关门了。

等了很久依然没有人，节目组准备载车带杨洋回去。

杨洋问节目组：是他们叫你来接我的吗？是谁说的？

这时候杨洋已经很不高兴了，试图问出是谁惦记自己。

结果没人惦记自己还没回来，所以杨洋拒绝了搭制作组的车，说气话：不来接就不来接呗，我不坐。

此时旅行才刚刚开始，杨洋还是小男生的赌气心理，没有意识到这个团体有多不和谐，后面领教过后就学乖了。

此时公寓里，许晴和郑爽开始闹矛盾了。郑爽一再阻止大家出门找杨洋，许晴语气很不好的说：郑爽你能成熟一点吗？

那天晚上，郑爽和许晴直接闹崩了。为什么呢？后来节目放出过两秒的片段回放，郑爽向许晴道歉：我觉得我现在说什么也没有用，我很喜欢你，希望你不要误会我。

许晴看也没看郑爽，直接转身就走，说：好的，我们有时间再聊。

郑爽主要是说话很混乱，无法正确表达自己内心想说的，还很消极，事情刚刚开始有点变坏，她就觉得都已经这样了，补救也没什么用了，所以让事情越来越糟。经过这件事，许晴迅速把郑爽划为不正常人。

其实在杨洋走丢前，大家还是很友善的。郑爽还准备买菜，惦记着许晴爱吃什么东西。

天色已经完全黑了，杨洋终于接受了不会有人来找自己的事实，于是开始乱走，找酒店。

其实杨洋走丢的那天，郑爽闹别扭，躲在窗帘后面哭了。这段被剪掉了，只在“下期看点”有过一秒的镜头。

许晴和郑爽闹矛盾后，一个人关在房间里。此时，先前被孤立的宁静开始抱团，夸赞郑爽不错，让郑爽别伤心。（毛阿敏和宁静这两个老大姐完全没有管过杨洋的事，只会说漂亮话）

杨洋依然没回来，郑爽下楼去拿外卖吃，在门外，郑爽和许晴对话。

郑爽问：我用去接杨洋吗？

许晴反问郑爽：你不是说不用接吗？

郑爽说：对啊，我本来就只是拿我的外卖来了。

许晴无语了，郑爽有点不知好歹的问：还要接他吗？

许晴：我当然认为需要接了！

这段不愉快的对话结束后，郑爽进门，井柏然准备出门。郑爽提议：我们就在这里等杨洋吧！

井柏然还是觉得需要去找杨洋，他跟郑爽
segments.title: 回顾花儿与少年第二季，它是如何从温馨崩成噩梦的？_郑爽

segments.text:
都说随便，有没有你们愿意住的？住帐篷还是房车？

结果郑爽来了一句：我哪都不爱住。 这句话让许晴很不爽，许晴本身就不喜欢郑爽，一句话都懒得搭理，来找她是解决问题的，而不是听郑爽说撒娇话的。

所以许晴也就直接挑明了：哪都不爱住是吧？那帐篷归我和毛阿敏住了。如果你们想住帐篷就去住，别说什么都可以什么都随便，那就别做事了。

许晴说完后，留下郑爽一个人心情复杂的待在原地。

说完自己想住帐篷后，许晴和毛阿敏准备开着车去买吃的，毕竟是户外露营。

许晴找到郑爽后，让郑爽她们把房车上的箱子拿下来，她们要开着房车去超市。

郑爽表示：这地方好脏。

宁静也帮助好姐妹郑爽：这灰特别大。言下之意：我们就不搬箱子。

而在一旁的毛阿敏并不知情，还对许晴说：我们开房车去买吃的，也要把车上的箱子拿下来啊。（箱子本身就是要拿下来的，晚上要露营，而且车重会耗油）

许晴撒气的说：她们不拿，说有灰，我真搞不懂。

说完后，许晴又对着毛阿敏吐槽：我问她们想住哪里，她们说随便，哪里都行，那帐篷就我们住吧，烦死人了。

郑爽错失帐篷，宁静拉着郑爽走到一旁，开始商量怎么把帐篷夺回来。

许晴在事后吐槽郑爽、宁静、陈意涵姐妹团，许晴说：我有点高估我自己，我有点累，那种累是因为一件很简单的事，她们说随便随便，让简单的事情复杂化，我特别不欣赏这样。

许晴还说：这个旅行还有九天才结束，我也不想逼着自己做那些她们觉得正常的行为。

我其实能理解许晴的心情，跟郑爽说话永远不在一个点上，郑爽永远在东拉西扯，一点也不真实，而许晴最反感虚伪。

吐槽归吐槽，在许晴说帐篷归自己和毛阿敏住以后，郑爽去打电话给爸妈，在电话里，郑爽说：晚上可能住帐篷吧。（看来郑爽心里还是放不下帐篷，势必要夺回来）

天色渐渐暗下来了，宁静看到制作方的帐篷，直接问：能住三个人吗？可以给我们吗？

宁静拿到帐篷后，还假意客套一番说：如果能睡三个人就睡女的，如果只能睡两个人，就睡男的。意思是：这不是为我搬过来的啊，我们很谦让，我们随意。

结果，车上还真的只找到两个睡袋，也就是说，这个帐篷归杨洋和井柏然睡了。

此时，许晴才姗姗来迟，她才知道宁静已经安排好了住宿，自己的提议被推翻了。

如果按照许晴的提议，是她和毛阿敏睡帐篷。但宁静直接推翻不认，说了N句随便后，又要求自己和郑爽、陈意涵睡帐篷。但如意算盘落空了，只有2个睡袋。于是帐篷只能让杨洋和井柏然睡。五个女人要一起睡在房车里。

许晴不愿意和抱团三姐妹睡在一起，说想安静一下。

于是，许晴直接在一辆小汽车的后座铺了个床，决定一个人度过一夜。

没多久，毛阿敏在房车上又多发现了一个睡袋，拿给了宁静。此刻，有了三个睡袋，宁静和郑爽如愿以偿的睡到了帐篷，还拉着陈意涵一起。

井柏然告诉许晴：她们三个住在帐篷里，不睡车上了。

许晴说：那好吧，我就回房车住了。

事后，陈意涵接受采访说：郑爽很想睡帐篷，她觉得住在车上很危险， 很多人在车上睡觉死了。

宁静的表现就更搞笑了，在镜头前说自己想睡在房车上。

宁静还表示：是陈意涵和郑爽想睡在帐篷，尤其是郑爽，要求一定不能主在车上。言下之意，宁静是为了陪着两姐妹才委屈住在帐篷里的。

人间作精宁静，这不行那不行，又作又想走耿直人设，“耿直”不是遮羞布，心机才是真的。

这段视频是两年后在网上火起来的，很多人觉得这是许晴洗白自己放出来的，但并不是。很搞笑，这段视频是郑爽的粉丝放出来的，为了是撕宁静，说宁静是两面派，坑郑爽。结果郑爽的两面派也被网友们发现了，这就是亲自给偶像招黑吧？

许晴拒绝共同用餐

通过抢帐篷事件，许晴更加认识到郑爽和宁静的两副面孔，很排斥她俩。抢帐篷的第二天，七个人要去吃午饭。

许晴直接不下车，不想跟三姐妹坐在一起，在车上等着大家吃完。

毛阿敏也心知肚明许晴不爽，于是说：那我给你打包一点吃的吧。

许晴坚持说：我真不吃。

大家津津有味的享用午饭

许晴真的不愿意吃饭吗？等到花少团吃完后，她跑到咖啡厅去享受食物了。她不是不饿，只是不想和抱团三姐妹坐在一起。

当时井柏然周旋在5个女人中间，直接急的叫了起来：无所谓，爱咋咋地吧，通过这一次，我对女人有新的了解。

试问，许晴有没有错。她有，她最大的错就是太拧巴，错在以为自己无所不能，以为真人秀里能交到真心的朋友，但当发现气场不对，没必要和她们成为朋友时，她连演都不想演，导致大家都被她的言语和行为弄得尴尬和小心翼翼，这是她最大的问题。

彻底撕破脸的篝火晚会

如果说房车事件是整个节目的高潮，那篝火晚会就是她们的决裂。

在抢帐篷后的第二天，花少团继续露营，宁静开心的扎帐篷

然而，郑爽坐在一旁默不作声，若有所思。

郑爽为什么心事重重的样子呢？因为连续两天晚上都要选房车和帐篷。虽然郑爽第一天如愿以偿的睡到了帐篷，但第二天起床后就担心晚上帐篷会被许晴抢走了。

于是郑爽刚起床就跟宁静、陈意涵说：我们还是继续睡帐篷吧，别想了。

陈意涵点头：那就说我们要睡帐篷。郑爽告诉她：我们就说睡出经验来了，有什么好说的啊？

佩服佩服，睡觉还能睡出经验来

房车之旅的第二天晚上，大家围在一起吃饭，旁边还有一堆篝火，毛阿敏提议玩真心话大冒险的游戏。这一段谈话非常的负能量和低气压。

宁静问井柏然：你最累的地方是什么？

井柏然说：大家都有自己的想法，有自己想做的事情，比如分房睡，我觉得是个很简单的事，大家弄得很复杂。大家都在说随便，到底是真的随便还是假的随便，我已经分不清了。最后，大家产生了很多误会。

杨洋问井柏然：这种情绪影响你多久了？

井柏然说：至今为止都会影响我，我今天已经快崩溃了。

井柏然又问陈意涵：你觉得这段旅行最沮丧的原因是什么？

陈意涵说：这个旅行和我想的不太一样。这两天一直有点事情，我也不晓得为什么。

陈意涵的意思是，他原本以为旅行会很轻松很美好，没想到如此的心累，这两天7个人里面有很多误会、排挤、冷落和争吵。

杨洋问郑爽：你觉得我们团队是刚开始融洽还是现在融洽？

郑爽说现在融洽。这句话也太假了··· 刚开始大家好歹还假客套一下，现在一个篝火晚会这么负能量，抢帐篷又这么心机，你跟我说融洽？

这次轮到每个人都问郑爽一个问题，大家让许晴提问，许晴直接说：我没有问题。这让本来就很冷的气氛变得更冷。

许晴说：有些人还是得有距离，真的不想再说第二句话，七个人的性格都不一样，要拼命融合在一起，又不可能融合，我真的好孤独。（这些话是后续采访时补上的）

现场的气氛很尴尬，轮到了大家问许晴问题。郑爽问：晴姐，你上季玩的开心还是这一季开心呀？

其实郑爽问这种问题真是没事找事，明知道许晴不喜欢她了还问，难不成非想看看许晴怎么发飙？得，许晴终于发飙了，气氛更尴尬了，就想问她为啥没事找事？

许晴不假思索的说：上一季。

本来依偎在许晴身边的井柏然惊恐的坐了起来，问许晴：为什么是上一季？

许晴说：因为上一季的人都正常。许晴四十多岁了，没有结婚生子，活在自己构想的艺术少女世界里。她对人际交往有种不切实际的高要求，拒绝市侩、讨巧、精明的交际。她真的不懂人情世故吗？她懂。她知道当自己说出这些话时现场气氛会更尴尬，但她不愿意虚伪的说那些。

毛阿敏一直坐在许晴身边，笑而不语的看着许晴说完了这些。我不喜欢毛阿敏这个做事风格，遇到团队成员之间的矛盾只会看热闹看笑话，很多事情争执不下时，往往大姐需要出来做出决定或者是处理矛盾，而不是袖手旁观。

当年这段播出时，很多人骂许晴。有些网友的识人眼光还是需要修炼。遇到那种敌对写在脸上的人你反而不用太担心，明枪易躲暗箭难防。反而是精于世故、平时看热闹、关键时刻做好人、好处全占齐的人才是应该最提防的。

宁静一直没有参加篝火晚会，看到导演拍的现场播放，感慨一句：怎么那么严肃的话题啊？

据说当时杨洋也说了一句话，但节目组为了突出许晴和郑爽的矛盾，那段话没有放出来。杨洋说的是：我在这里并不快乐，因为每个人都是冰冷的。

后续采访时，宁静也很不满许晴，她说：有跟自己个性不一样的人在身边，就那么不舒服吗？那有没有想过，我在别人身边，别人也会不舒服我呢？

我说难听点，如果说宁静和许晴是两坨各不相干的shi，那郑爽就是那根搅屎棍，没有她在中间瞎作，宁静和许晴压根不会有正面冲突。

篝火晚会上，每个人心里都有鬼，有的人把这趟旅行当个秀敷衍了事，比如郑爽和宁静，嘴上说一套，心里想一套。但有的人把这次当成旅行相处真情实感，比如许晴，该说什么就是什么，明知道气氛全掌握在自己的一句话，却依然不违心说话。

郑爽和宁静暗戳戳的内涵小彩蛋

许晴已经在明面上撕宁静、郑爽、陈意涵的小团体了，小团体当然也不会放过许晴。

某天晚上，宁静在敷面膜，郑爽在一旁跟宁静聊天：你看晴姐不是第二次来了嘛，让她当导游不是更好吗？有经验了，当导演是最见证能力的，她肯定也想锻炼自己，不然她为什么要来呢？下一站我们推荐一下许晴当导游吧。

宁静在旁边和郑爽一唱一和。

郑爽还明知故问：她会不会怕自己做不好啊？

宁静回：谁都怕自己做不好。

当导游是件很累的事，郑爽经常说自己在英国给大家当导游时很崩溃，井柏然也说自己当导游很累。郑爽心知肚明这些，却依然笑嘻嘻的提议许晴当导游，你觉得她是抱着什么态度去提的呢？

老大姐毛阿敏的哭泣晚餐

我们再来说说毛阿敏，毛阿敏和许晴也不是多好的朋友，不过是在一群心怀鬼胎的人里互相取暖的一对。但当许晴和别人发生一些矛盾，你又被迫选择跟她站在一边，这就导致你和其他人的疏远，根本不利于正常的友谊发展。

于是，在篝火晚会事件后后，毛阿敏在饭桌上冷落了许晴，向宁静、陈意涵和郑爽大献殷勤。

许晴很看不惯，直接离席走人了。

许晴为什么走？她的回答是：我觉得那个大桌

# 11年后，全网重审内娱名著《花少2》

出品 | 虎嗅青年文化组

作者 | 黄瓜汽水

编辑 | 渣渣郡

《花儿与少年》是芒果台推出的一档旅行综艺节目，邀请不同年龄段的七位明星共同踏上异国旅程，节目组会为他们设置不同难度的集体活动，摄像机全程记录明星之间的化学反应。

然而，唯有第二季《花少》，达到了前无古人后无来者的节目效果。

11年前录制节目的时候，天不时地不利人不和，一档节目竟然集齐了七位性格迥异的明星。

11年后这档节目翻红，反而占尽了天时地利人和。所有人都站在宣传节点上，共同将这档2015年的节目送上2026年的热搜榜。

毛阿敏上了最新一期《歌手》；井柏然播出新剧《早春晴朗》；宁静在直播间接住流量玩起了狼人杀；如今已经是“海外素人”的郑爽在TikTok更新动态。多位当事人同时出现，让大家再次重温诸神之战。

更重要的是，芒果台新一季《花儿与少年》上线，很难不让人怀疑这是节目组的自我营销。

**平台助推、宣发操盘，用户二创，一切都是最坏的安排。**

11年来，“花学”经久不衰，其学科分支包括社会学、心理学、沟通学、人类学、家庭关系学。

在B站，“花学索引派”的解读视频突然被送上流量高峰，几万人同时在线收看，甚至凌晨4点在线人数都高达2000人。

一恨鲥鱼多刺，二恨海棠无香，三恨红楼未完，四恨《花少2》母带不能问世。

11年前，明星在综艺里争得你死我活；11年后，观众为了各自阵营火热开战。

《花少2》之后，再也没有一档综艺节目，能让每一位参与嘉宾都觉得自己被孤立了。

几位明星从勉强体面走向癫狂撕逼的精神状态，甚至可以拿来形容自己人生的奥德赛：

“我现在的人生正处于郑爽进不去民宿时期，陈意涵车站问路被丢下时期，杨洋剑桥走丢时期，宁静不想爬伦敦桥时期，井柏然搬13件行李时期，许晴管毛大姐要钥匙时期，毛大姐见经纪人时期，井柏然听到许晴上一季玩的开心突然从许晴肩膀弹起来幸福者退让时期。”

几大著名战役，如今细细品读，仍然余味悠长。11年间，不少花学家亲自前往战役遗址打卡，纪念这段人类史上最糟糕的团队关系。

伦敦桥战役风雨飘摇，注定了这个团队八字不合的天崩开局。

伦敦桥战役亲历者 网友@艺艺子Julia（携宠自驾ing）

杨洋剑桥走失事变，是整个《花少2》的二战转折点。

整个团队动态平衡，每个人都游走在推诿、甩锅、拒绝担责之间，每个环节都推动了矛盾爆发。

明明在地图上仅仅十几分钟的路程，一屋子人愣是磨叽了半天也不去接。也就是那天不搬行李，不然杨洋不超过五分钟就被接回来了。

房车大战更是凸显人性幽微。

根据网友考据，当时郑爽认为睡在房车里会死人，用一句低情商发言“我哪都不愿意住”点燃了老公主许晴的怒火。于是抢夺帐篷入住权成为当时两个小团体的巅峰之战。

只能说，如果少一根引信都不会产生如此炸裂的化学反应，低情商遇到高敏感，公主病邂逅焦虑症。

逼得最没有存在感的艺人陈意涵学会了幸福者退让原则，一遇到大场面就出门跑步躲风头。

每位嘉宾都在2026年迎接了自己的妙梗。

许晴是定语从句女王。著名的参考语料为：“我信任的、交心的、交流的、心与心的、我爱的毛毛姐，我不认识了。”

毛阿敏是邪恶斜刘海。在井柏然搬行李箱的时候，她的几句场面话被观众反复拷打：“小井啊，你要是我儿子我心疼死了”，网友给她又加了一句台词：“可惜你不是，快搬箱子去。”

杨洋从刚到伦敦时的纯真期待，到剑桥走丢后的满脸困惑，宛如新兵蛋子误入二战前线，表情转变完美概括了年轻人“初入社会vs被社会暴揍”的精神状态。

理论上来讲，目前不在内娱就业的海外素人郑爽，是唯一一个能为大家还原案发现场的当事人，但碍于她的语言表达水平堪忧，恐怕也说不清到底发生了什么。

“盘点那些死前还在笑的角色”

这是综艺史上唯一一档“原教旨主义全员恶人”的节目。

宁静伦敦桥悟道、陈意涵地铁站走丢悟道、井柏然搬行李箱悟道、毛阿敏鸿门宴悟道、许晴沙场悟道。

至于杨洋，可能是在11年后的抖音里才悟道。所有名场面，他要么睡着了，要么听不懂，要么大家懒得理他，他知道的未必有网友多。

伦敦文旅局就应该趁热打铁，推出一个伦敦桥限定七人剧本杀。

七位嘉宾甚至惨出了一丝团魂，苦出了一丝恨海情天的况味。

运动量拉满，睡眠不足，满伦敦暴走，剑桥划船拉练，徒步爬山睡户外，帐篷不够还要抢，前期食物仅能果腹。

在体力崩盘的同时，还要积极勾心斗角。只可惜伦敦的枕头大战没有放到最后一期，不然每个人都要偷偷给枕头里塞砖头。

《花少2》才是真正被综艺之神眷顾的节目。因为神来了都救不了。

别的节目都是恶剪，花少2是善剪。剪出这么多炸裂的场面，竟然还是对艺人的保护。我们仍未知晓中途退出到底要赔多少违约金。

代入任何一家粉丝你都会痛苦，但如果你是乐子人，反而会因为明星撕得披头散发而笑得合不拢嘴。

《花少2》的七人组在舆论场上经历的起起伏伏，只证明了一件事：**互联网是回合制的，没有绝对的好人。**

没有人能逃得过被逐帧分析，每个人都要经历被送上被告席的过程。作为观众，你会感觉“似乎谁说得都有道理”。

最早被出击的，可以追溯到目前暂时最无辜的杨洋。

2023年，杨洋由于在电视剧《我的人间烟火》饰演宋焰被全网群嘲。当时他的罪名是油腻巨婴，甚至还有人根据他坐在路边的体态以及花坛的实际高度来推算他的真实身高。

三年之后，口碑迎来全面反转，杨洋反而成了最阳光快乐没心眼之人。

腥风血雨间，只有他在专心经营自己的呆萌生活。其他人激情团战的时候，他在厕所看《阿衰》蹲到腿麻。

接下来是毛阿敏。

由于up主 @读心者新一 的解读最早出圈，暗示了整个节目的隐藏boss是大姐毛阿敏：毛阿敏拉拢了许晴，把许晴当枪使。许晴当众暴雷后，毛为了避免落单迅速割席。许晴遭背刺和抛弃，沙场悟道成功复仇。

由于每次冲突毛阿敏都带着迷之微笑审视全场，从每一次冲突中全身而退，被网友评价为“一个歌手给六个演员上了23天的免费大师课”。

然而，仅仅半个月时间，审判就迎来了反转。网友开始了“大拉表”清洗行动：谁干的活最多，谁干的活最少，咱们数据上见。

毛阿敏竟然在毫无营销助力的情况下，靠群众的雪亮双眼洗清冤屈。

大众立场跟着营销号走，一天换一个靶子，三天不上网，你都不知道新的网暴对象轮到了谁。

**我信任的，交心的，交流的，心与心的，我爱的网友们，全都变脸了。**

今天毛阿敏是被群嘲的大姐，德艺1.5馨；明天就是节目组虐待老人，让一个50多岁有腰伤的中老年人开手动档皮卡开了7个小时，最后连顶帐篷也没落着。网友揶揄这是“人老了买营销公关都比别人慢半拍”。

真正看完原片的人都知道，毛阿敏一路承担了翻译、做饭、问路、开车的工作，徒步时照顾好自己不拖团队后腿，几次主动给年轻人收拾垃圾。节目最后还落个“闲人毛大姐”的称号，可谓是出力不讨好。

职场里最忌讳这种人设：工作不留痕，默默干完所有脏活累活，嘴笨不卖惨，最后还要承担骂名。

“毛毛姐你要是我妈妈我心疼死了。可惜你不是，继续开车去吧。”

为毛阿敏平反后，观众反手又将许晴送上审判席。

当年，一句“上一季的人都正常”打响花学第一枪，这句名言时至今日仍然高悬在中国综艺最高峰。

在“大拉表行动”中，许晴干活最少，得分最低。她的罪名是社会化程度低，自我意识过剩，随时随地自嬷为大院公主，毫无团队意识。

还有网友挖出了陈意涵早期的采访，疑似许晴嫌弃陈意涵烤焦了面包，进一步坐实了她的公主病。

共情许晴的人，

# Tavily search integration

Integrate with the Tavily search tool using LangChain Python.

[Tavily’s Search API](https://tavily.com) is a search engine built specifically for AI agents (LLMs), delivering real-time, accurate, and factual results at speed.

## [​](#overview) Overview

### [​](#integration-details) Integration details

| Class | Package | Serializable | [JS support](https://js.langchain.com/docs/integrations/tools/tavily_search) | Version |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [`TavilySearch`](https://reference.langchain.com/python/langchain-tavily/tavily_search/TavilySearch) | [`langchain-tavily`](https://reference.langchain.com/python/langchain-tavily/) | ✅ | ✅ |

### [​](#tool-features) Tool features

| [Returns artifact](/oss/python/langchain/tools) | Native async | Return data | Pricing |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ❌ | ✅ | title, URL, content snippet, raw\_content, answer, images | 1,000 free searches / month |

## [​](#setup) Setup

The integration lives in the `langchain-tavily` package.

```
pip install -qU langchain-tavily pip install - qU langchain - tavily
```

### [​](#credentials) Credentials

We also need to set our Tavily API key. You can get an API key by visiting [this site](https://app.tavily.com/sign-in) and creating an account.

```
import getpass import  getpass import os import  os if not os.environ.get("TAVILY_API_KEY"): if  not  os. environ. get("TAVILY_API_KEY"): os.environ["TAVILY_API_KEY"] = getpass.getpass("Tavily API key:\n")  os. environ[" TAVILY_API_KEY "] =  getpass. getpass("Tavily API key: \n ")
```

## [​](#instantiation) Instantiation

Here we show how to instantiate an instance of the Tavily search tool. The tool accepts various parameters during instantiation:

* max\_results (optional, int): Maximum number of search results to return. Default is 5.
* topic (optional, str): Category of the search. Can be “general”, “news”, or “finance”. Default is “general”.
* include\_answer (optional, bool): Include an answer to original query in results. Default is False.
* include\_raw\_content (optional, bool): Include cleaned and parsed HTML of each search result. Default is False.
* include\_images (optional, bool): Include a list of query related images in the response. Default is False.
* include\_image\_descriptions (optional, bool): Include descriptive text for each image. Default is False.
* search\_depth (optional, str): Depth of the search, either “basic” or “advanced”. Default is “basic”.
* time\_range (optional, str): The time range back from the current date to filter results - “day”, “week”, “month”, or “year”. Default is None.
* include\_domains (optional, List[str]): List of domains to specifically include. Default is None.
* exclude\_domains (optional, List[str]): List of domains to specifically exclude. Default is None.

## [​](#invocation) Invocation

### [​](#invoke-directly-with-args) [Invoke directly with args](/oss/python/langchain/tools)

The Tavily search tool accepts the following arguments during invocation:

* `query` (required): A natural language search query
* The following arguments can also be set during invocation: `include_images`, `search_depth`, `time_range`, `include_domains`, `exclude_domains`
* For reliability and performance reasons, certain parameters that affect response size cannot be modified during invocation: `include_answer` and `include_raw_content`. These limitations prevent unexpected context window issues and ensure consistent results.

NOTE: The optional arguments are available for agents to dynamically set, if you set an argument during instantiation and then invoke the tool with a different value, the tool will use the value you passed during invocation.

```
tool.invoke({"query": "What happened at the last wimbledon"}) tool. invoke({"query":  "What happened at the last wimbledon"})

# Coroutines and tasks[¶](#coroutines-and-tasks "Link to this heading")

This section outlines high-level asyncio APIs to work with coroutines and Tasks.

## [Coroutines](#id2)[¶](#coroutines "Link to this heading")

**Source code:** [Lib/asyncio/coroutines.py](https://github.com/python/cpython/tree/3.15/Lib/asyncio/coroutines.py)

---

[Coroutines](../glossary.html#term-coroutine) declared with the async/await syntax is the preferred way of writing asyncio applications. For example, the following snippet of code prints “hello”, waits 1 second, and then prints “world”:

```
>>> import  asyncio>>> async def  main():... print('hello')... await asyncio. sleep(1)... print('world')>>> asyncio. run(main()) hello world
```

Note that simply calling a coroutine will not schedule it to be executed:

```
>>> main() 
```

To actually run a coroutine, asyncio provides the following mechanisms:

* The [`asyncio.run()`](asyncio-runner.html#asyncio.run "asyncio.run") function to run the top-level entry point “main()” function (see the above example.)
* Awaiting on a coroutine. The following snippet of code will print “hello” after waiting for 1 second, and then print “world” after waiting for *another* 2 seconds:

  ```
   import  asyncio import  time async def  say_after(delay, what): await asyncio. sleep(delay) print(what) async def  main(): print(f "started at {time. strftime(' %X ')} ") await say_after(1, 'hello') await say_after(2, 'world') print(f "finished at {time. strftime(' %X ')} ") asyncio. run(main())
  ```

  Expected output:

  ```
   started at 17: 13: 52 hello world finished at 17: 13: 55
  ```
* The [`asyncio.create_task()`](#asyncio.create_task "asyncio.create_task") function to run coroutines concurrently as asyncio [`Tasks`](#asyncio.Task "asyncio.Task").

  Let’s modify the above example and run two `say_after` coroutines *concurrently*:

  ```
   async def  main(): task1 = asyncio. create_task(say_after(1, 'hello')) task2 = asyncio. create_task(say_after(2, 'world')) print(f "started at {time. strftime(' %X ')} ")# Wait until both tasks are completed (should take# around 2 seconds.) await task1 await task2 print(f "finished at {time. strftime(' %X ')} ")
  ```

  Note that expected output now shows that the snippet runs 1 second faster than before:

  ```
   started at 17: 14: 32 hello world finished at 17: 14: 34
  ```
* The [`asyncio.TaskGroup`](#asyncio.TaskGroup "asyncio.TaskGroup") class provides a more modern alternative to [`create_task()`](#asyncio.create_task "asyncio.create_task"). Using this API, the last example becomes:

  ```
   async def  main(): async with asyncio. TaskGroup() as tg: task1 = tg. create_task(say_after(1, 'hello')) task2 = tg. create_task(say_after(2, 'world')) print(f "started at {time. strftime(' %X ')} ")# The await is implicit when the context manager exits. print(f "finished at {time. strftime(' %X ')} ")
  ```

  The timing and output should be the same as for the previous version.

  Added in version 3.11: [`asyncio.TaskGroup`](#asyncio.TaskGroup "asyncio.TaskGroup").

## [Awaitables](#id3)[¶](#awaitables "Link to this heading")

We say that an object is an **awaitable** object if it can be used in an [`await`](../reference/expressions.html#await) expression. Many asyncio APIs are designed to accept awaitables.

There are three main types of *awaitable* objects: **coroutines**, **Tasks**, and **Futures**.

Coroutines

Python coroutines are *awaitables* and therefore can be awaited from other coroutines:

```
 import  asy

on 3.14: Passes on all *kwargs* to [`loop.create_task()`](asyncio-eventloop.html#asyncio.loop.create_task "asyncio.loop.create_task")

    cancel()[¶](#asyncio.TaskGroup.cancel "Link to this definition")
    :   Cancel the task group. This is a non-exceptional, early exit of the task group’s lifetime – useful once the group’s goal has been met or its services no longer needed.

        [`cancel()`](#asyncio.Task.cancel "asyncio.Task.cancel") will be called on any tasks in the group that aren’t yet done, as well as the parent (body) of the group. The task group context manager will exit *without* [`asyncio.CancelledError`](asyncio-exceptions.html#asyncio.CancelledError "asyncio.CancelledError") being raised.

        If `cancel()` is called before entering the task group, the group will be cancelled upon entry. This is useful for patterns where one piece of code passes an unused [`asyncio.TaskGroup`](#asyncio.TaskGroup "asyncio.TaskGroup") instance to another in order to have the ability to cancel anything run within the group.

        `cancel()` is idempotent and may be called after the task group has already exited.

        Some ways to use `cancel()`:

        * call it from the task group body based on some condition or event
        * pass the task group instance to child tasks via [`create_task()`](#asyncio.create_task "asyncio.create_task"), allowing a child task to conditionally cancel the entire group
        * pass the task group instance or bound `cancel()` method to some other task *before* opening the task group, allowing remote cancellation

        Added in version 3.15.

Example:

```
 async def  main(): async with asyncio. TaskGroup() as tg: task1 = tg. create_task(some_coro(...)) task2 = tg. create_task(another_coro(...)) print(f"Both tasks have completed now: {task1. result()}, {task2. result()} ")
```

The `async with` statement will wait for all tasks in the group to finish. While waiting, new tasks may still be added to the group (for example, by passing `tg` into one of the coroutines and calling `tg.create_task()` in that coroutine). There is also opportunity to request termination of the entire task group with `tg.cancel()`, based on some condition. Once the last task has finished and the `async with` block is exited, no new tasks may be added to the group.

The first time any of the tasks belonging to the group fails with an exception other than [`asyncio.CancelledError`](asyncio-exceptions.html#asyncio.CancelledError "asyncio.CancelledError"), the remaining tasks in the group are cancelled. No further tasks can then be added to the group. At this point, if the body of the `async with` statement is still active (i.e., [`__aexit__()`](../reference/datamodel.html#object.__aexit__ "object.__aexit__") hasn’t been called yet), the task directly containing the `async with` statement is also cancelled. The resulting `asyncio.CancelledError` will interrupt an `await`, but it will not bubble out of the containing `async with` statement.

Once all tasks have finished, if any tasks have failed with an exception other than [`asyncio.CancelledError`](asyncio-exceptions.html#asyncio.CancelledError "asyncio.CancelledError"), those exceptions are combined in an [`ExceptionGroup`](../builtins/exceptions.html#ExceptionGroup "ExceptionGroup") or [`BaseExceptionGroup`](../builtins/exceptions.html#BaseExceptionGroup "BaseExceptionGroup") (as appropriate; see their documentation) which is then raised.

Two base exceptions are treated specially: If any task fails with [`KeyboardInterrupt`](../builtins/exceptions.html#KeyboardInterrupt "KeyboardInterrupt") or [`SystemExit`](../builtins/exceptions.html#SystemExit "SystemExit"), the task group still cancels the remaining tasks and waits for them, but then the initial `KeyboardInterrupt` or `SystemExit` is re-raised instead of [`ExceptionGroup`](../builtins/exceptions.html#ExceptionGroup "ExceptionGroup") or [`BaseExceptionGroup`](../builtins/exceptions.html#BaseExceptionGroup

segments.text:
"BaseExceptionGroup").

If the body of the `async with` statement exits with an exception (so [`__aexit__()`](../reference/datamodel.html#object.__aexit__ "object.__aexit__") is called with an exception set), this is treated the same as if one of the tasks failed: the remaining tasks are cancelled and then waited for, and non-cancellation exceptions are grouped into an exception group and raised. The exception passed into `__aexit__()`, unless it is [`asyncio.CancelledError`](asyncio-exceptions.html#asyncio.CancelledError "asyncio.CancelledError"), is also included in the exception group. The same special case is made for [`KeyboardInterrupt`](../builtins/exceptions.html#KeyboardInterrupt "KeyboardInterrupt") and [`SystemExit`](../builtins/exceptions.html#SystemExit "SystemExit") as in the previous paragraph. There is an additional special case made only for the body of the `async with`: if it raises [`GeneratorExit`](../builtins/exceptions.html#GeneratorExit "GeneratorExit") and none of the other tasks raise exceptions that would be reported, then the `GeneratorExit` is reraised.

Task groups are careful not to mix up the internal cancellation used to “wake up” their [`__aexit__()`](../reference/datamodel.html#object.__aexit__ "object.__aexit__") with cancellation requests for the task in which they are running made by other parties. In particular, when one task group is syntactically nested in another, and both experience an exception in one of their child tasks simultaneously, the inner task group will process its exceptions, and then the outer task group will receive another cancellation and process its own exceptions.

In the case where a task group is cancelled externally and also must raise an [`ExceptionGroup`](../builtins/exceptions.html#ExceptionGroup "ExceptionGroup"), it will call the parent task’s [`cancel()`](#asyncio.Task.cancel "asyncio.Task.cancel") method. This ensures that a [`asyncio.CancelledError`](asyncio-exceptions.html#asyncio.CancelledError "asyncio.CancelledError") will be raised at the next [`await`](../reference/expressions.html#await), so the cancellation is not lost.

Task groups preserve the cancellation count reported by [`asyncio.Task.cancelling()`](#asyncio.Task.cancelling "asyncio.Task.cancelling").

Changed in version 3.13: Improved handling of simultaneous internal and external cancellations and correct preservation of cancellation counts.

Changed in version 3.15: Addition of the special case for [`GeneratorExit`](../builtins/exceptions.html#GeneratorExit "GeneratorExit").

## [Sleeping](#id7)[¶](#sleeping "Link to this heading")

*async* asyncio.sleep(*delay*, *result=None*)[¶](#asyncio.sleep "Link to this definition")
:   Block for *delay* seconds.

    If *result* is provided, it is returned to the caller when the coroutine completes.

    `sleep()` always suspends the current task, allowing other tasks to run.

    Setting the delay to 0 provides an optimized path to allow other tasks to run. This can be used by long-running functions to avoid blocking the event loop for the full duration of the function call.

    Example of coroutine displaying the current date every second for 5 seconds:

    ```
     import  asyncio import  datetime  as  dt async def  display_date(): loop = asyncio. get_running_loop() end_time = loop. time() +5.0 while True: print(dt. datetime. now()) if(loop. time() +1.0)>= end_time: break await asyncio. sleep(1) asyncio. run(display_date())
    ```

    Changed in version 3.10: Removed the *loop* parameter.

    Changed in version 3.13: Raises [`ValueError`](../builtins/exceptions.html#ValueError "ValueError") if *delay* is [`nan`](math.html#math.nan "math.nan").

# Traces

The path of a request through your application.

**Traces** give us the big picture of what happens when a request is made to an application. Whether your application is a monolith with a single database or a sophisticated mesh of services, traces are essential to understanding the full “path” a request takes in your application.

Let’s explore this with three units of work, represented as [Spans](#spans):

### Spans

A **span** represents a single unit of work or operation. Spans track specific operations that a request makes, painting a picture of what happened during the time in which that operation was executed.

A span contains name, time-related data, [structured log messages](/docs/concepts/signals/traces/#span-events), and [other metadata (that is, Attributes)](/docs/concepts/signals/traces/#attributes) to provide information about the operation it tracks.

#### Span attributes

Span attributes are metadata attached to a span.

The following table contains examples of span attributes:

| Key | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `http.request.method` | `"GET"` |
| `network.protocol.version` | `"1.1"` |
| `url.path` | `"/webshop/articles/4"` |
| `url.query` | `"?s=1"` |
| `server.address` | `"example.com"` |
| `server.port` | `8080` |
| `url.scheme` | `"https"` |
| `http.route` | `"/webshop/articles/:article_id"` |
| `http.response.status_code` | `200` |
| `client.address` | `"192.0.2.4"` |
| `client.socket.address` | `"192.0.2.5"` (the client goes through a proxy) |
| `user_agent.original` | `"Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64; rv:72.0) Gecko/20100101 Firefox/72.0"` |

For more on spans and how they relate to OpenTelemetry, see [Spans](/docs/concepts/signals/traces/#spans).

### Distributed traces

A **distributed trace**, more commonly known as a **trace**, records the path taken by a single request (made by an application or end user) as it propagates through multiple services in an architecture, such as microservice or serverless applications.

A trace is made of one or more spans. The first span represents the root span. Each root span represents a request from start to finish. The spans underneath the parent provide a more in-depth context of what occurs during a request (or what steps make up a request).

For example, when a user loads a web page, the initial HTTP request may pass through an API gateway, a backend service, and a database. Each of these steps is represented by a span, and together they form a single trace that shows the end-to-end journey of the request.

Without tracing, finding the root cause of performance problems in a distributed system can be challenging. Tracing makes debugging and understanding distributed systems less daunting by breaking down what happens within a request as it flows through a distributed system.

Many Observability backends visualize traces as waterfall diagrams that look like this:

![Sample Trace](/img/waterfall-trace.svg "Trace waterfall diagram")

Waterfall diagrams show the parent-child relationship between a root span and its child spans. When a span encapsulates another span, this also represents a nested relationship.

For more on traces and how they pertain to OpenTelemetry, see [Traces](/docs/concepts/signals/traces/).

`TaskGroup` 的关键不是 `create_task`，而是 `async with`。它告诉读者和解释器：

**这些任务属于同一个并发作用域。离开这个作用域之前，所有任务必须结束。**

这和文件操作里的 `with open(...)` 很像。你不需要在每个分支里手动关闭文件，因为上下文管理器会兜底；你也不需要手动收尾每个异步任务，因为 `TaskGroup` 会在退出时等待它们。

### [](https://blog.csdn.net/windowshht/article/details/161408696)[](https://blog.csdn.net/windowshht/article/details/161408696)三、取消传播：失败不是孤立事件

现在看一个更真实的例子：一个任务失败，其他任务会怎样？

```python
import asyncio

async def slow_worker(name: str):
    try:
        print(f"{name}: start")
        await asyncio.sleep(5)
        print(f"{name}: done")
    finally:
        print(f"{name}: cleanup")

async def broken_worker():
    print("broken_worker: start")
    await asyncio.sleep(0.5)
    raise RuntimeError("remote service failed")

async def main():
    try:
        async with asyncio.TaskGroup() as tg:
            tg.create_task(slow_worker("worker-A"))
            tg.create_task(slow_worker("worker-B"))
            tg.create_task(broken_worker())
    except* RuntimeError as group:
        print(f"caught RuntimeError group: {group}")

asyncio.run(main())
```

任务可以便捷和安全地取消。 当任务被取消时，[`asyncio.CancelledError`](asyncio-exceptions.html#asyncio.CancelledError "asyncio.CancelledError") 将在遇到机会时在任务中被引发。

推荐协程使用 `try/finally` 代码块来可靠地执行清理逻辑。 对于 [`asyncio.CancelledError`](asyncio-exceptions.html#asyncio.CancelledError "asyncio.CancelledError") 被显式捕获的情况，它通常应当在清理完成时被传播。 `asyncio.CancelledError` 会直接子类化 [`BaseException`](../builtins/exceptions.html#BaseException "BaseException") 因此大多数代码都不需要关心这一点。

启用结构化并发的 asyncio 组件，如 [`asyncio.TaskGroup`](#asyncio.TaskGroup "asyncio.TaskGroup") 和 [`asyncio.timeout()`](#asyncio.timeout "asyncio.timeout")，在内部是使用撤销操作来实现的因而在协程屏蔽了 [`asyncio.CancelledError`](asyncio-exceptions.html#asyncio.CancelledError "asyncio.CancelledError") 时可能无法正常工作。 类似地，用户代码通常也不应调用 [`uncancel`](#asyncio.Task.uncancel "asyncio.Task.uncancel")。 但是，在确实想要屏蔽 `asyncio.CancelledError` 的情况下，则还有必要调用 `uncancel()` 来完全移除撤销状态。

Developers must introduce mutex and synchronization mechanisms to protect against race conditions, but the correctness of such mitigations is difficult to verify and must be considered whenever making adjustments to the code or even calling it.

> *You have to have a level of vigilance bordering on paranoia just to make sure that your conventions around where state can be manipulated and by whom are honoured, because when such an interaction causes a bug it’s nearly impossible to tell where it came from.*
>
> *—* [*Glyph, Unyielding*](https://blog.glyph.im/2014/02/unyielding.html)

Coroutines differ from threads in that they implement cooperative multitasking—they must yield control or suspend explicitly (e.g. via a yield or await statement). This means that the programmer is always aware of a potential context switch and is able to arrange a graceful and safe suspension. Glyph [compares](https://blog.glyph.im/2014/02/unyielding.html) this sort of statement to a relief valve: a single clearly marked point where we have to consider the implications of a potential transfer of control. As such, coroutines can be thought of as a semantic improvement over threads.

## The problem of runaway tasks

Despite the convenience of coroutine-based concurrency, Python's asyncio module has long lacked an intuitive and convenient way to manage groups of concurrently running tasks. The current API revolves around [*create\_task*](https://docs.python.org/3.11/library/asyncio-task.html#asyncio.create_task), which returns a task handle to the user. The user is then responsible for keeping references to running tasks, collecting return values, and handling safe cancellation in case of errors. This is notoriously difficult and prone to errors. The lack of correct task management leads to runaway tasks, which never get awaited by the parent or checked for exceptions. As a result, the program can easily end up in an invalid state while failing to emit any kind of error or warning.

Consider the following code:

```
async def(): asyncio create_task(coro_a()) task_b asyncio create_task(coro_b()) Arbitrary computation here return await task_a
```

```
async def(): asyncio create_task(coro_a()) task_b asyncio create_task(coro_b()) Arbitrary computation here return await task_a
```

```
async def(): asyncio create_task(coro_a()) task_b asyncio create_task(coro_b()) Arbitrary computation here return await task_a
```

```
async def(): asyncio create_task(coro_a()) task_b asyncio create_task(coro_b()) Arbitrary computation here return await task_a
```

```
async def(): asyncio create_task(coro_a()) task_b asyncio create_task(coro_b()) Arbitrary computation here return await task_a
```

The parent task spawns two child tasks, **A** and **B**, and lets them run in the background. Eventually, it awaits the completion of **A**. Once **A** is done, it either produces a return value or propagates an exception into the call stack. However, **B** is never awaited, which is not strictly wrong, but it exposes us to the following scenarios:

* The task dies without our knowledge. Seemingly unrelated code may deadlock or start misbehaving, as it assumes that the task is running in the background.
* We expect the task to have ended, but a bug in its termination logic makes it run silently in the background, causing unexpected behavior elsewhere.

Both situations are nightmares to debug. Once the example function exits, **B** becomes orphaned—we lose our reference to the task and are no longer able to manage its lifetime.

## UTC Started in the Seventies

Coordinated Universal Time in its present form was **officially adopted on January 1, 1972**.

The concept was developed by the International Radio Consultative Committee (CCIR) in the early sixties. In 1967, the International Telecommunication Union (ITU) officially adopted the name UTC, and in 1970, international agreements were reached to set the legal framework for its worldwide implementation.

[Why it’s so hard to convert time zones in your head](https://www.timeanddate.com/time/convert-time-zones-in-your-head.html)
## GMT Used to Be the Global Standard

Although UTC in its present form has only been around for a few decades, the general idea of using a universal time standard to anchor local times worldwide was first put into practice **as early as 1884**: At the International Meridian Conference, delegates from 25 countries designated **Greenwich Mean Time (GMT) as the reference point**.

## An Unusual Abbreviation

You may have noticed that the letters UTC don’t reflect the order of the words **C**oordinated **U**niversal **T**ime.

[Find out why](https://www.timeanddate.com/time/utc-abbreviation.html)

This historical decision is why GMT is still occasionally used as a substitute for UTC today.

At the time, GMT was **based on Earth’s rotation**—specifically, on the mean solar time at the [prime meridian](https://www.timeanddate.com/geography/prime-meridian-wrong.html), which runs through the Royal Observatory in Greenwich, [London](https://www.timeanddate.com/worldclock/uk/london).

With [advances in timekeeping technology](https://www.timeanddate.com/time/history-of-timekeeping.html) and the need for a more precise and stable global time standard, **UTC eventually replaced GMT**. Today, GMT is just another time zone derived from UTC and is no longer based on solar time in Greenwich.

# UTC: The World’s Time Standard

Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) is the basis for civil time in all time zones worldwide.

Image 2: Portrait of AnneImage 3: Portrait of Konstantin

By Anne Buckle and Konstantin Bikos

Share this article

Image 4: Time zone map illustration showing time zones for the whole world.

The time in every time zone worldwide is defined by its difference, or offset, from UTC. 

©timeanddate.com

## Point of Reference for Local Times Everywhere

UTC is the time standard commonly used to determine local times around the world. Every time zone is defined by its difference from UTC, known as its UTC offset. [...] For example, the local time in China is eight hours ahead of UTC, so China Standard Time has a UTC offset of UTC+8. When it’s 09:00 UTC, clocks in Beijing show 17:00 (5:00 pm).

Our complete guide to UTC offsetsUTC offsets of all time zones

Image 5: Illustrated map of the world's time zones. Time Zone Map Current local times around the world, including (DST) changes.

## UTC Offset Can Shift

While every time zone has a fixed UTC offset, some countries jump back and forth from one time zone to another every year, so the local UTC offset shifts accordingly.

This may sound strange, but if you live in a country that observes Daylight Saving Time (DST), shifting your UTC offset is precisely what you do every time you spring ahead or fall back. [...] People in New York, for example, follow Eastern Standard Time (EST) during part of the year. It’s five hours behind UTC, so the offset is UTC-5. In early March, clocks go ahead by one hour to Eastern Daylight Time (EDT), reducing the offset to UTC-4.

If you’re the visual type, check out our Time Zone Map—it reflects all DST changes worldwide in real time.

## 24-Hour Notation

While you’re free to state any time around the world using the 12-hour time format with “am” and “pm” labels, UTC always uses the 24-hour clock, also known as military time.

For example, 7 o’clock in the evening must be written as 19:00 UTC. It is incorrect to write 7:00 pm UTC.

12-hour to 24-hour conversion chartISO 8601 is the global standard for time and date formats

### GMT: Same, but Different [...] ### GMT: Same, but Different

You may have seen Greenwich Mean Time (GMT) being used as a reference point instead of UTC. In practice, it doesn’t make any difference: GMT and UTC share the same current time, so both offsets are the same. Technically, however, it’s wrong: GMT is a time zone, not a time standard.

More importantly, it can lead to confusion. You see, GMT is generally associated with the local time in the UK—as the name suggests, it reflects the time in Greenwich, London. What some people don’t realize is that the UK doesn’t observe GMT during the Daylight Saving Time period, when Brits turn their clocks to British Summer Time (BST).

BST is one hour ahead of GMT (UTC+1). If you fail to account for that, your time zone conversion will be one hour off.

Advertising [...] Advertising  

## How UTC Is Measured

Given that so much depends on UTC, it’s no surprise that significant effort goes into ensuring its precision.

Two components are used to keep it ticking at exactly the right pace:

   International Atomic Time (TAI): A time scale that combines the output of some 450 highly precise atomic clocks worldwide.  
   Universal Time (UT1): Also known as astronomical time or solar time, it refers to the Earth’s rotation. It is used to compare the pace provided by TAI with the actual length of a day on Earth.  

To reconcile the ultra-precise speed of atomic clocks with the fluctuations of Earth’s rotation, a leap second is added to or removed from UTC when the difference between the two components is predicted to reach 0.9 seconds within 12 months.

東海道・山陽新幹線を直通する速達タイプの列車が「のぞみ」号です。新大阪～博多間の所要時間は2時間28分程度です。

Title: 杭州：早春二月的西湖十景，花港无鱼、苏堤未晓春_断桥残雪_雷峰塔_天气
# 杭州：早春二月的西湖十景，花港无鱼、苏堤未晓春. 西湖十景是形成于南宋时期、基本围绕西湖分布的十处特色风景，包括：苏堤春晓、曲院风荷、平湖秋月、断桥残雪、柳浪闻莺、花港观鱼、雷峰夕照、双峰插云、南屏晚钟、三潭印月。. 用了两天徒步西湖，找全了西湖十景。二月下旬，不是旅游季节，看到的西湖十景和旅游季不太一样：苏堤未晓春，花港无鱼，没有柳浪没有莺，断桥有残雪……。. 不期而遇的平湖秋月。从浙江博物馆孤山馆出来，等公交还得半小时，决定步行才遇到“平湖秋月”。. 湖，的确宽阔、“平坦”，平如镜；天气，是早春二月的阴雨天气；下午，无月。. 终于是个好天，虽然还是挺凉。柳树未绿，柳枝在风中舞动，有喜鹊没有莺。. 三潭映月有人说是西湖三个湖心岛，不对！是这样三个“小葫芦”状的石塔。相传为苏东坡在杭疏浚西湖时所创设（现有石塔为明代重建）。塔腹中空，球面体上排列着五个等距离圆洞，若在月明之夜，洞口糊上薄纸，塔中点燃灯光，洞形印入湖面。每个塔里都有5个“小月亮”，三个塔就是15个；倒映到水里，那就是30个“小月亮”。一轮天上的明月和其湖中的倒影，这就是32轮月亮了！. 仅在杭州几天，能遇到下雪算是运气爆棚。知道南方的雪很难站住，早早地赶到断桥去看“断桥残雪”。. 断桥，就是一座挺普通的石拱桥，雪天里也没觉得怎么美啊！即便传说美，景色也并不美。. “断桥残雪”美的秘密在这里，是站在断桥上看湖边的宝石山。保叔塔和山上的树被薄雪覆盖。在断桥上望过去就是一幅极美的水墨山水画。. 老雷峰塔在1924年就倒塌了，鲁迅还写过《论雷峰塔的倒掉》。小时候读过此文，对雷峰塔的印象就很深。现在的雷峰塔是2002年重建的。. 遇到下雪，为了看西湖雪景，从断桥赶到雷峰塔。还好，残雪还在。. 这个景点和雷峰塔就隔着马路。一首叫“南屏晚钟”的歌，还有杨万里那首“晓出净慈寺送林子方”的诗，是不是都和这个景点有关？现在的净慈寺一看就是新建的。不时，也传出悠扬的钟声。. “双峰插云”的碑亭在，环视四周，‘双峰’连影子也没看到啊。. 上一次去杭州还是98年，时间就是这么快，二十多年转瞬过。上次肯定也游西湖，但一点印象都没有了。所以，随手写写游记还是很必要的：记忆会忘却，文字随时可以翻阅。.

segments.text: # 西湖新十景，西湖新十景有哪些景点名字. ## 西湖旧十景和新十景. 〖壹〗、 “西湖十景”是西湖上的十处特色风景，分别是苏堤春晓、曲院风荷、平湖秋月、断桥残雪、柳浪闻莺、花港观鱼、雷峰夕照、双峰插云、南屏晚钟、三潭印月。西湖十景形成于南宋时期，基本围绕西湖分布，有的就位于湖上。. 〖贰〗、 西湖旧十景指的是：云溪竹径、九溪烟树、虎跑梦泉、黄龙吐翠、满陇桂雨、玉皇飞云、龙井问茶、宝石流霞、吴山天风、阮墩环碧。. 〖叁〗、 西湖十景分别是哪十景西湖“旧十景”指的是苏堤春晓、曲苑风荷、平湖秋月、断桥残雪、柳浪闻莺、花港观鱼、雷峰夕照、双峰插云、南屏晚钟、三潭印月。. 〖肆〗、 西湖旧十景指的是2007年之前的十景：云溪竹径、九溪烟树、虎跑梦泉、黄龙吐翠、满陇桂雨、玉皇飞云、龙井问茶、宝石流霞、吴山天风、阮墩环碧。. 〖伍〗、 杭州“西湖十景”是苏堤春晓、曲院风荷、平湖秋月、断桥残雪、柳浪闻莺、花港观鱼、雷峰夕照、双峰插云、南屏晚钟、三潭印月。. ## 新西湖十景新西湖十景是哪十景,简要介绍. 〖壹〗、 西湖十景分别为：苏堤春晓、曲院风荷、平湖秋月、断桥残雪、花港观鱼、柳浪闻莺、三潭印月、双峰插云、雷峰夕照、南屏晚钟。. 〖贰〗、 西湖十景是：苏堤春晓 此景为西湖十景之首。苏提俗称苏公提，北宋诗人苏东坡主持疏浚西湖工程时取湖泥葑草铸成，横贯湖南北，将西湖分成内外两部分。苏堤在西湖西南侧，南起南屏路，北接曲院风荷，全长8公里。. 〖叁〗、 “西湖十景”其名借自南宋的山水画，它是西湖自然景观的主要内涵，融进了南宋以来画师们对西湖景色的充分认识。. 〖肆〗、 新西湖十景是1985年经过杭州市民及各地群众积极参与评选，并由专家评选委员会反复斟酌后确定的，它们是：云栖竹径、满陇桂雨、虎跑梦泉、龙井问茶、九溪烟树、吴山天风、阮墩环碧、黄龙吐翠、玉皇飞云、宝石流霞。. 〖伍〗、 “西湖十景”指的是苏堤春晓、曲院风荷、平湖秋月、断桥残雪、柳浪闻莺、花港观鱼、雷峰夕照、双峰插云、南屏晚钟、三潭印月这十处景色。. 〖陆〗、 西湖十景是：断桥残雪、西湖晨雾、曲院风荷、三潭印月、莫干山绿水、花港观鱼、蘇堤春晓、宝石流连、黄龙吐翠、云栖竹径。西湖景区中有名的前十 风景名胜。. ## 杭州西湖二十景?? 〖壹〗、 其实西湖最著名的一共有三十景，其中二十景是前边的旧十景和新十景，剩下十景是南宋时候的苏堤春晓、曲苑风荷、平湖秋月、断桥残雪、柳浪闻莺、花港观鱼、雷峰夕照、双峰插云、南屏晚钟、三潭印月。. 〖贰〗、 “西湖十景”是西湖上的十处特色风景，分别是苏堤春晓、曲院风荷、平湖秋月、断桥残雪、柳浪闻莺、花港观鱼、雷峰夕照、双峰插云、南屏晚钟、三潭印月。西湖十景形成于南宋时期，基本围绕西湖分布，有的就位于湖上。. 〖叁〗、 苏堤自北宋始建至今，一直保持了沿堤两侧相间种植桃树和垂柳的植物景观特色。春季拂晓是欣赏“苏堤春晓”的最佳时间，此时薄雾蒙蒙，垂柳初绿、桃花盛开，尽显西湖旖旎的柔美气质。. ## 西湖十景是哪十景. 西湖十景包括苏堤春晓、曲院风荷、平湖秋月、断桥残雪、柳浪闻莺、花港观鱼、雷峰夕照、双峰插云、南屏晚钟和三潭印月。西湖十景形成于南宋时期，基本围绕西湖分布，有的就位于西湖之上，是人类与自然和谐共处的产物。. 西湖十景有曲院风荷、苏堤春晓、平湖秋月、断桥残雪、花港观鱼、柳浪闻莺、三潭印月、双峰插云、雷峰夕照、南屏晚钟。. 西湖十景有：苏堤春晓、曲院风荷、平湖秋月、断桥残雪、花港观鱼、柳浪闻莺、三潭印月、双峰插云、雷峰夕照、南屏晚钟。. 西湖十景名为：苏堤春晓、曲院风荷、平湖秋月、断桥残雪、花港观鱼、柳浪闻莺、三潭印月、双峰插云、雷峰夕照、南屏晚钟。. 西湖十景是指苏堤春晓、曲院风荷、平湖秋月、断桥残雪、花港观鱼、南屏晚钟、双峰插云、雷峰夕照、三潭印月以及柳浪闻莺这十个景点。西湖十景是位于中国浙江省杭州市西湖区境内一组代表性的景点，共分布在周围的十处特色景区。.

# [Readiness probe](/t/readiness-probe/34826)

When a readiness Probe failed, kubernetes remove the Pod from the service point so that traffic could not move toward that pod. Pod remain in the node. Kubernetes continues to run the readiness probe checks against the container. If the application recovers and the readiness probe passes again, Kubernetes automatically re-adds the pod to the service endpoints to resume traffic.  
If the pod remain failed in readiness probe, it is of no use in and only consuming the Node CPU and memory. Then why kubernetes do not kill the pod and remove it from the Node? Why there is no time frame to check the readiness probe failure after which the Pod should be removed from the node?

Hello Qazaidi,

If you’d like your container to be killed and restarted if a probe fails, then specify a liveness probe, and specify a `restartPolicy` of `Always` or `OnFailure`

`restartPolicy`
`Always`
`OnFailure`

The liveness probe passes when the app itself is healthy, but the readiness probe additionally checks that each required back-end service is available. This helps you avoid directing traffic to Pods that can only respond with error messages.

**WHY?**  
If you want to notice the difference between an app that has failed and an app that is still processing its startup data, you might prefer a readiness probe.

Thanks,  
Manan

If a container does not provide a particular probe, the kubelet always considers the result as `Success`. For readiness probes specifically, the result is considered `Failure` before the initial delay.

## Configuration fields

[Probes](/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.37/#probe-v1-core) have a number of fields that you can use to more precisely control the behavior of startup, liveness and readiness checks. For example:

```
apiVersion: v1 kind: Pod metadata:  name: probe-example spec:  containers:  - name: app  image: registry.k8s.io/e2e-test-images/agnhost:2.40  ports:  - containerPort: 8080  startupProbe:  httpGet:  path: /healthz  port: 8080  failureThreshold: 30  periodSeconds: 10  livenessProbe:  httpGet:  path: /healthz  port: 8080  initialDelaySeconds: 10  periodSeconds: 5  timeoutSeconds: 3  failureThreshold: 3  readinessProbe:  httpGet:  path: /ready  port: 8080  periodSeconds: 5 
```

`initialDelaySeconds`
:   Number of seconds after the container has started before startup, liveness or readiness probes are initiated. If a startup probe is defined, liveness and readiness probe delays do not begin until the startup probe has succeeded. In some older Kubernetes versions, the initialDelaySeconds might be ignored if periodSeconds was set to a value higher than initialDelaySeconds. However, in current versions, initialDelaySeconds is always honored and the probe will not start until after this initial delay. Defaults to 0 seconds. Minimum value is 0.

`periodSeconds`
:   How often (in seconds) to perform the probe. Default to 10 seconds. The minimum value is 1. While a container is not Ready, the readiness probe may be executed at times other than the configured `periodSeconds` interval. This is to make the Pod ready faster.

`timeoutSeconds`
:   Number of seconds after which the probe times out. Defaults to 1 second. Minimum value is 1.

`successThreshold`
:   Minimum consecutive successes for the probe to be considered successful after having failed. Defaults to 1. Must be 1 for liveness and startup Probes. Minimum value is 1.

`failureThreshold`
:   After a probe fails `failureThreshold` times in a row, Kubernetes considers that the overall check has failed: the container is *not* ready/healthy/live. Defaults to 3. Minimum value is 1. For the case of a startup or liveness probe, if at least `failureThreshold` probes have failed, Kubernetes treats the container as unhealthy and triggers a restart for that specific container. The kubelet honors the setting of `terminationGracePeriodSeconds` for that container. For a failed readiness probe, the kubelet continues running the container that failed checks, and also continues to run more probes; because the check failed, the kubelet sets the `Ready` [condition](/docs/concepts/workloads/pods/pod-lifecycle/#pod-conditions) on the Pod to `false`.

`terminationGracePeriodSeconds`
:   configure a grace period for the kubelet to wait between triggering a shut down of the failed container, and then forcing the container runtime to stop that container. The default is to inherit the Pod-level value for `terminationGracePeriodSeconds` (30 seconds if not specified), and the minimum value is 1. See [probe-level `terminationGracePeriodSeconds`](#probe-level-terminationgraceperiodseconds) for more detail.

#### Caution:

Incorrect implementation of readiness probes may result in an ever growing number of processes in the container, and resource starvation if this is left unchecked.

# Zero-downtime Deployment in Kubernetes with Jenkins

By **[Kaitlyn Barnard](https://github.com/kbarnard10)** |

Ever since we added the [Kubernetes Continuous Deploy](https://aka.ms/azjenkinsk8s) and [Azure Container Service](https://aka.ms/azjenkinsacs) plugins to the Jenkins update center, "How do I create zero-downtime deployments" is one of our most frequently-asked questions. We created a quickstart template on Azure to demonstrate what zero-downtime deployments can look like. Although our example uses Azure, the concept easily applies to all Kubernetes installations.

## Rolling Update

Kubernetes supports the RollingUpdate strategy to replace old pods with new ones gradually, while continuing to serve clients without incurring downtime. To perform a RollingUpdate deployment:

* Set `.spec.strategy.type` to `RollingUpdate` (the default value).
* Set `.spec.strategy.rollingUpdate.maxUnavailable` and `.spec.strategy.rollingUpdate.maxSurge` to some reasonable value.
  + `maxUnavailable`: the maximum number of pods that can be unavailable during the update process. This can be an absolute number or percentage of the replicas count; the default is 25%.
  + `maxSurge`: the maximum number of pods that can be created over the desired number of pods. Again this can be an absolute number or a percentage of the replicas count; the default is 25%.
* Configure the `readinessProbe` for your service container to help Kubernetes determine the state of the pods. Kubernetes will only route the client traffic to the pods with a healthy liveness probe.

We'll use deployment of the official Tomcat image to demonstrate this:

```
apiVersion: extensions/v1beta1 kind: Deployment metadata: name: tomcat-deployment-rolling-update spec: replicas: 2 template: metadata: labels: app: tomcat role: rolling-update spec: containers: - name: tomcat-container image: tomcat:${TOMCAT_VERSION} ports: - containerPort: 8080 readinessProbe: httpGet: path: / port: 8080 strategy: type: RollingUpdate rollingUp maxSurge: 50% 
```

If the Tomcat running in the current deployments is version 7, we can replace `${TOMCAT_VERSION}` with 8 and apply this to the Kubernetes cluster. With the [Kubernetes Continuous Deploy](https://aka.ms/azjenkinsk8s) or the [Azure Container Service](https://aka.ms/azjenkinsacs) plugin, the value can be fetched from an environment variable which eases the deployment process.

Behind the scenes, Kubernetes manages the update like so:

* Initially, all pods are running Tomcat 7 and the frontend Service routes the traffic to these pods.
* During the rolling update, Kubernetes takes down some Tomcat 7 pods and creates corresponding new Tomcat 8 pods. It ensures:
  + at most `maxUnavailable` pods in the desired Pods can be unavailable, that is, at least (`replicas` - `maxUnavailable`) pods should be serving the client traffic, which is 2-1=1 in our case.
  + at most maxSurge more pods can be created during the update process, that is 2\*50%=1 in our case.
* One Tomcat 7 pod is taken down, and one Tomcat 8 pod is created. Kubernetes will not route the traffic to any of them because their readiness probe is not yet successful.
* When the new Tomcat 8 pod is ready as determined by the readiness probe, Kubernetes will start routing the traffic to it. This means during the update process, users may see both the old service and the new service.
* The rolling update continues by taking down Tomcat 7 pods and creating Tomcat 8 pods, and then routing the traffic to the ready pods.
* Finally, all pods are on Tomcat 8.

The Rolling Update strategy ensures we always have some Ready backend pods serving client requests, so there's no service downtime. However, some extra care is required:

* During the update, both the old pods and new pods may serve the requests. With
